title: Chapter 21 — Passeriformes
description: The largest order of birds, containing over 6,000 species — more than half of all bird species on Earth. Passerines are defined by a specialised foot with three toes pointing forward and one back, locking automatically when the bird perches. The order includes the songbirds, whose complex vocalisations are produced by a uniquely elaborate syrinx.

children.name: Cephalopyrus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Fire-capped Tit, a small greenish-yellow tit of the Himalayan foothills with a brilliant orange-red crown patch. It was once placed in the penduline tit family Remizidae but molecular studies place it firmly within Paridae.

children.name: Parus
children.description: The great tits — large, bold members of the family with striking black-and-yellow plumage and a versatile, opportunistic diet. The Great Tit is one of the most studied birds in the world, a model organism for research into ecology, behaviour, and the evolutionary consequences of urbanisation. Its two-note song is famously variable and can be rendered in dozens of dialects across its range.

children.name: Parus major
children.description: The great tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is widespread and common throughout Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and as far east as the Amur River. It also occurs in parts of North Africa where it is generally resident in any sort of woodland.

children.name: Parus minor
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus cinereus
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus bokharensis
children.description: The great tit (Parus major) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Cyanistes
children.description: The blue tits — small, acrobatic tits with vivid blue-and-yellow plumage. The Eurasian Blue Tit (Blåmes) is one of the most familiar garden birds across Europe, famous for its ability to hang upside-down on the outermost branches to reach insects, and for its habit of opening milk bottle tops — a learned behaviour that spread across Britain in the 20th century.

children.name: Cyanistes caeruleus
children.description: The Eurasian blue tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is easily recognised by its blue and yellow plumage and small size.

children.name: Cyanistes cyanus
children.description: The azure tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout Russia, Central Asia, northwest China, Manchuria, and Pakistan.

children.name: Periparus
children.description: Small, dark tits of coniferous forests, distinguished by their glossy black cap and bib. The Coal Tit is the most widespread, a diminutive bird that hoards food in winter — tiny caches of seeds and insects secreted in bark crevices, which it can remember and retrieve weeks later.

children.name: Periparus ater
children.description: The coal tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in forests throughout the temperate to subtropical Palearctic, including North Africa. The black-crested tit is now included in this species.

children.name: Pardaliparus
children.description: Small, brightly coloured tits of East and Southeast Asian forests, formerly included in Periparus. The Yellow-bellied Tit is one of the most beautiful members of the family, resembling a living jewel with its black-and-yellow plumage and white crescent on the nape.

children.name: Pardaliparus elegans
children.description: The elegant tit (Periparus elegans) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Pardaliparus amabilis
children.description: The Palawan tit (Periparus amabilis) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile
children.description: Marsh and willow tits of the northern Palearctic — drab but charming birds in brown and white, best told apart by their calls. The Willow Tit excavates its own nest hole in rotten wood, while the Marsh Tit takes over existing cavities. The Siberian Tit is one of the hardiest passerines on Earth, surviving Arctic winters through shivering, food caching, and a remarkably high metabolic rate. In North America the genus includes the chickadees, among the most familiar and beloved backyard birds on the continent.

children.name: Poecile palustris
children.description: The marsh tit is a Eurasian passerine bird in the tit family Paridae and genus Poecile, closely related to the willow tit, Père David's and Songar tits. It is a small bird, around 12 cm (4.7 in) long and weighing 12 g (0.42 oz), with a black crown and nape, pale cheeks, brown back and greyish-brown wings and tail. Between 8 and 11 subspecies are recognised.

children.name: Poecile montanus
children.description: The willow tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout temperate and subarctic Europe and across the Palearctic. The plumage is grey-brown and off-white with a black cap and bib.

children.name: Poecile lugubris
children.description: The sombre tit (Poecile lugubris) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Paridae, the "true" tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile cinctus
children.description: The grey-headed chickadee or Siberian tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread resident breeder throughout subarctic Scandinavia and the northern Palearctic, and also into North America in Alaska and the far northwest of Canada. It is a conifer specialist.

children.name: Poecile carolinensis
children.description: The Carolina chickadee (Poecile carolinensis) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile gambeli
children.description: The mountain chickadee (Poecile gambeli) is a small songbird, a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile hudsonicus
children.description: The boreal chickadee (Poecile hudsonicus) is a small passerine songbird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile sclateri
children.description: The Mexican chickadee (Poecile sclateri) is a small passerine songbird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile weigoldicus
children.description: The Sichuan tit (Poecile weigoldicus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile songarus
children.description: The Songar tit (Poecile montanus songarus) is a passerine bird in the tit family.

children.name: Sittiparus
children.description: Varied tits of East Asia, recently split from Poecile based on genetic and morphological differences. These are colourful, pattern-faced tits restricted to islands and coastal regions of Japan, Taiwan, and eastern China.

children.name: Sittiparus varius
children.description: The varied tit (Sittiparus varius) is a perching bird from the tit family, Paridae.

children.name: Sittiparus ierardi
children.description: Endemic to the Izu Islands south of Tokyo, this tit differs from the Varied Tit in its darker belly and reduced white on the face. It is a restricted-range species vulnerable to introduced predators.

children.name: Sylviparus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Yellow-browed Tit, a tiny, olive-green leaf-gleaning tit of Asian forests with a distinct warbler-like appearance and habits.

children.name: Lophophanes
children.description: Crested tits — recognisable at a glance by their spiky, black-and-white crest, unique among European tits. The Crested Tit is a specialist of mature pine forests and rarely strays far from them, making it one of the few European birds that cannot easily recolonise areas after deforestation. It too caches food extensively through winter.

children.name: Lophophanes cristatus
children.description: The crested tit or European crested tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in coniferous forests throughout central and northern Europe and in deciduous woodland in France and the Iberian Peninsula. In Great Britain, it is mainly restricted to the ancient pinewoods of Inverness and Strathspey in Scotland, and rarely strays far from its haunts.

children.name: Machlolophus
children.description: Yellow-crested tits of South and East Asia, with striking sulphur-yellow crests and underparts. They inhabit broadleaf and mixed forests from the foothills of the Himalayas to the islands of Japan and Taiwan, filling a similar ecological niche to the great tits of the western Palearctic.

children.name: Machlolophus holsti
children.description: The yellow tit (Machlolophus holsti), also known as Taiwan yellow tit and Formosan yellow tit is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Machlolophus xanthogenys
children.description: The Himalayan black-lored tit (Machlolophus xanthogenys), also known as simply black-lored tit, is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus
children.description: African black tits — the continent's dominant tit group, replacing the Eurasian Parus in sub-Saharan Africa. Most species are predominantly black with white or yellow markings, and many show striking white wing patches. They are active, acrobatic foragers in acacia savanna, miombo woodland, and montane forest across the whole of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Melaniparus funereus
children.description: thumb|Dusky Tit The dusky tit (Melaniparus funereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus semilarvatus
children.description: A large, glossy black tit with a large white shoulder patch, endemic to the lowland forests of West Africa. It is a specialised forest interior species, scarce and local throughout its range.

children.name: Melaniparus griseiventris
children.description: The miombo tit (Melaniparus griseiventris) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus cinerascens
children.description: The ashy tit (Melaniparus cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus afer
children.description: The grey tit (Melaniparus afer) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Pseudopodoces
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ground Tit of the Tibetan Plateau — a remarkable bird long classified as a crow relative due to its terrestrial habits and decurved bill. Molecular analysis revealed it to be a highly modified parid that has adapted to life above the treeline, nesting in rodent burrows and feeding on invertebrates in the sparse alpine steppe.

children.name: Pseudopodoces humilis
children.description: The ground tit, Tibetan ground tit, or Hume's ground tit (Pseudopodoces humilis) is a bird of the Tibetan plateau north of the Himalayas.

children.name: Baeolophus
children.description: The titmice of North America — small grey crested tits that are bold, vocal visitors to woodlands and feeders across the United States and Mexico.

children.name: Baeolophus bicolor
children.description: The tufted titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor) is a small songbird native to eastern North America.

children.name: Baeolophus inornatus
children.description: thumb|Oak Titmouse, Auburn, California The oak titmouse (Baeolophus inornatus) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Baeolophus wollweberi
children.description: The bridled titmouse (Baeolophus wollweberi) is a small passerine bird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Baeolophus ridgwayi
children.description: The juniper titmouse (Baeolophus ridgwayi) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melanochlora
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Sultan Tit, by far the largest member of the family, a crested black-and-yellow giant of Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Melanochlora sultanea
children.description: The sultan tit (Melanochlora sultanea) is an Asian forest bird with black upperparts plumage and yellow underparts, dark bill, and (depending on subspecies) a yellow or black crest.

children.name: Aphelocoma
children.description: Scrub-jays — crrestless, blue-and-grey jays of North and Central America, inhabiting scrubby oak woodland, chaparral, and semi-arid habitats. They are notable for their exceptional episodic memory: Western Scrub-Jays remember what, where, and when they cached food, and take account of whether a rival was watching when they hid it — a cognitive feat that implies an awareness of other minds.

children.name: Aphelocoma californica
children.description: The California scrub jay (Aphelocoma californica) is a species of scrub jay native to western North America.

children.name: Aphelocoma coerulescens
children.description: The Florida scrub jay (Aphelocoma coerulescens[A]) is one of the species of scrub jay native to North America..

children.name: Aphelocoma insolaris
children.description: A scrub-jay of the interior western United States, found in pinyon-juniper and scrub oak habitats from Oregon to Texas. Distinguished from the California scrub-jay by its duller plumage and more restricted blue markings.

children.name: Aphelocoma insularis
children.description: The island scrub jay (Aphelocoma insularis), also known as the island jay or Santa Cruz jay, is a bird in the genus, Aphelocoma, which is endemic to Santa Cruz Island off the coast of Southern California.

children.name: Aphelocoma ultramarina
children.description: The Transvolcanic jay (Aphelocoma ultramarina) , is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays..

children.name: Aphelocoma unicolor
children.description: The unicolored jay (Aphelocoma unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays..

children.name: Aphelocoma woodhouseii
children.description: Woodhouse's scrub jay (Aphelocoma[a] woodhouseii) is a species of scrub jay native to western North America, ranging from southeastern Oregon and southern Idaho to central Mexico..

children.name: Calocitta
children.description: Calocitta — a genus of crows, ravens & magpies in the family Corvidae.

children.name: Calocitta colliei
children.description: The black-throated magpie-jay (Cyanocorax colliei) is a strikingly long-tailed magpie-jay of northwestern Mexico..

children.name: Calocitta formosa
children.description: The white-throated magpie-jay (Cyanocorax formosus) is a large Central American species of magpie-jay..

children.name: Cissa
children.description: Green magpies — small, brilliantly coloured corvids of South and Southeast Asian forests, with vivid emerald-green plumage (which fades to turquoise or blue in captivity due to a diet-dependent carotenoid pigment), bright red bill and legs, and a chestnut wing panel. They are secretive inhabitants of forest understorey and mid-storey, where their coloration provides effective camouflage against sunlit foliage.

children.name: Cissa chinensis
children.description: The common green magpie (Cissa chinensis) is a member of the crow family, roughly the size of the Eurasian jay or slightly smaller.

children.name: Cissa hypoleuca
children.description: The Indochinese green magpie (Cissa hypoleuca), also known as the yellow-breasted magpie, is a small colourful bird native to the forests of China and Vietnam..

children.name: Cissa jefferyi
children.description: The Bornean green magpie (Cissa jefferyi) is a passerine bird in the crow family, Corvidae..

children.name: Cissa thalassina
children.description: The Javan green magpie (Cissa thalassina) is a passerine bird in the crow family, Corvidae, endemic to montane forests on the island of  Western Java, Indonesia..

children.name: Coloeus
children.description: Jackdaws — compact, sociable corvids with pale eyes and a distinctive silver-grey nape. Among the most social corvids, they form long-term pair bonds, nest colonially, and regularly follow larger ungulates and humans to catch disturbed insects. The Eurasian Jackdaw's silver eye gives it an unusually expressive, inquisitive gaze.

children.name: Coloeus monedula
children.description: The western jackdaw, also known as the Eurasian jackdaw, the European jackdaw, or simply the jackdaw, is a passerine bird in the crow family. It is found across Europe, western Asia and western North Africa; it is mostly resident, although northern and eastern populations migrate south in the winter. Four subspecies are recognised, which differ mainly in the darker or paler greyscale of the plumage on the head and nape.

children.name: Coloeus dauuricus
children.description: The Daurian jackdaw (Coloeus dauuricus) is a bird in the crow family, Corvidae, native to eastern Asia.

children.name: Corvus
children.description: Crows and ravens — the largest and most wide-ranging genus in the family, with an almost global distribution. Corvus species are renowned for problem-solving, social complexity, and long memory for individual human faces. The Common Raven is the largest passerine and one of the most intelligent birds known, capable of planning, deception, and playful behaviour.

children.name: Aphelocoma coerulescens
children.description: The Florida scrub jay (Aphelocoma coerulescens[A]) is one of the species of scrub jay native to North America..

children.name: Aphelocoma insularis
children.description: The island scrub jay (Aphelocoma insularis), also known as the island jay or Santa Cruz jay, is a bird in the genus, Aphelocoma, which is endemic to Santa Cruz Island off the coast of Southern California.

children.name: Corvus albicollis
children.description: The white-necked raven (Corvus albicollis), also known as the collared raven, is a species of raven native to eastern and southern Africa..

children.name: Corvus albus
children.description: The pied crow (Corvus albus) is a widely distributed African bird species in the crow genus of the family Corvidae.

children.name: Corvus bennetti
children.description: The little crow (Corvus bennetti) is an Australian species of crow, very similar to the Torresian crow in having white bases to the neck and head feathers (shown when ruffled in strong wind) but slightly smaller (38–45 cm in length) and with a slightly smaller bill.

children.name: Corvus brachyrhynchos
children.description: The American crow is a large passerine bird species of the family Corvidae. It is a common bird found throughout much of North America, only absent from the tundra biome. The American crow is the New World counterpart to the carrion crow and the hooded crow of Eurasia, occupying similar ecological niches.

children.name: Corvus capensis
children.description: The Cape crow or black crow (Corvus capensis) is slightly larger (48–50 cm in length) than the carrion crow and is completely black with a slight gloss of purple in its feathers.

children.name: Corvus capitalis
children.description: A large jungle crow of the Indian subcontinent, with a heavy bill and glossy black plumage.

children.name: Corvus celebensis
children.description: The Sulawesi crow (Corvus celebensis) is a passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae that is endemic to the Indonesian island of Sulawesi.

children.name: Corvus corax
children.description: The common raven or northern raven is a large all-black passerine bird. It is the most widely distributed of all corvids, found across the Northern Hemisphere. There are 11 accepted subspecies with little variation in appearance, although recent research has demonstrated significant genetic differences among populations from various regions.

children.name: Corvus cornix
children.description: The hooded crow, also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow in the genus Corvus. Widely distributed, it is found across Northern, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe, as well as parts of the Middle East. It is an ashy-grey bird with black head, throat, wings, tail, and thigh feathers, as well as a black bill, eyes, and feet.

children.name: Corvus corone
children.description: The carrion crow is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic. Along with the hooded crow, the carrion crow occupies a similar ecological niche in Eurasia to the American crow in North America. The two species look very similar to one another, but can be differentiated by size, as the carrion crow is larger and of a stockier build compared to the American crow.

children.name: Corvus coronoides
children.description: The Australian raven (Corvus coronoides) is a passerine corvid bird native to Australia.

children.name: Corvus crassirostris
children.description: The thick-billed raven (Corvus crassirostris) is a large passerine bird in the family Corvidae..

children.name: Corvus cryptoleucus
children.description: The Chihuahuan raven (Corvus cryptoleucus) is a species in the family Corvidae that is native to the United States and Mexico.

children.name: Corvus cubanus
children.description: A medium-sized crow endemic to Cuba and the Isla de la Juventud, where it inhabits palm savannas and forests. Its call is a distinctive, nasal 'caw' that differs notably from that of mainland North American crows.

children.name: Corvus dauuricus
children.description: The Daurian jackdaw (Coloeus dauuricus) is a bird in the crow family, Corvidae, native to eastern Asia.

children.name: Corvus edithae
children.description: thumb|Somali Crow The Somali crow, or dwarf raven (Corvus edithae), is approximately the size (44–46 cm in length) of the carrion crow, Corvus corone but with a longer bill and a somewhat more brownish cast to the feathers, especially when worn.

children.name: Corvus enca
children.description: The Sunda crow (Corvus enca) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae that is found in South-East Asia, from Malaysia to Borneo.

children.name: Corvus florensis
children.description: The Flores crow (Corvus florensis) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.

children.name: Corvus frugilegus
children.description: The rook is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds. It is found in the Palearctic, its range extending from Scandinavia and western Europe to eastern Siberia. It is a large, gregarious, black-feathered bird, distinguished from similar species by the whitish featherless area on the face.

children.name: Corvus fuscicapillus
children.description: The brown-headed crow is a passerine bird of the genus Corvus in the family Corvidae. Endemic to Indonesia, it has a fragmented distribution in subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest. It is threatened by habitat destruction and the IUCN has rated it as being "Least Concern".

children.name: Corvus haitiensis
children.description: A small crow of Haiti, darker and glossier than the palm crow.

children.name: Corvus hawaiiensis
children.description: The Hawaiian crow or ʻalalā is a species of bird in the crow family, Corvidae, that is currently extinct in the wild, though reintroduction programs are underway. It is about the size of the carrion crow at 48–50 cm (19–20 in) in length, but with more rounded wings and a much thicker bill. It has soft, brownish-black plumage and long, bristly throat feathers; the feet, legs, and bill are black.

children.name: Corvus imparatus
children.description: The Tamaulipas crow (Corvus imparatus) is a crow found in northeastern Mexico and southern Texas..

children.name: Corvus imperatus
children.description: A large, powerful crow of the Himalayan foothills and mountain forests from Pakistan to Myanmar. Its deep, resonant call echoes through mountain valleys at dawn. Sometimes treated as a subspecies of the jungle crow, but morphological and vocal differences support full species status.

children.name: Corvus imperialis
children.description: A large crow of the Moluccas, the largest Corvus in the region with a heavy, arched bill.

children.name: Corvus insolens
children.description: A crow of the Bismarck Archipelago with a short, thick bill and deep, resonant call.

children.name: Corvus jamaicensis
children.description: The Jamaican crow (Corvus jamaicensis) is a comparatively small corvid (35–38 cm in length).

children.name: Corvus kubaryi
children.description: The Mariana crow (Corvus kubaryi) ( ) is a species of the crow family from the tropical Western Pacific.

children.name: Corvus leucognaphalus
children.description: The white-necked crow is the largest of the four Caribbean corvids. It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola ; it was formerly also extant on Puerto Rico and Saint Croix in the United States Virgin Islands, but has been extirpated from both islands due to considerable forest clearance and hunting for meat.

children.name: Corvus leucognathalus
children.description: A medium-sized crow of Hispaniola and Puerto Rico. The white base of the neck feathers (often concealed) and the bluish-white iris distinguish it from other Caribbean crows.

children.name: Corvus leucognathus
children.description: A crow of Hispaniola and Puerto Rico with white-based neck feathers, visible when ruffled.

children.name: Corvus levaillantii
children.description: The large-billed crow, formerly referred to widely as the jungle crow, is a widespread Asian species of crow. It is very adaptable and is able to survive on a wide range of food sources, making it capable of colonizing new areas, due to which it is often considered a nuisance, especially on islands. It has a large bill, which is the source of its scientific name macrorhynchos and it is sometimes known by the common name thick-billed crow.

children.name: Corvus macrorhynchos
children.description: The large-billed crow (Corvus macrorhynchos), formerly referred to widely as the jungle crow, is a widespread Asian species of crow..

children.name: Corvus meeki
children.description: The Bougainville crow (Corvus meeki) is a species of bird in the crow family, Corvidae..

children.name: Corvus mekongensis
children.description: A recent species described from the Mekong River basin of Cambodia and Vietnam. Its ecology is poorly known but it is believed to favour riverine forest and agricultural areas in the Mekong floodplain.

children.name: Corvus mellori
children.description: The little raven is a species of the family Corvidae that is native to southeastern Australia. An adult individual is about 48–50 cm (19–19.5 in) in length, with completely black plumage, beak, and legs; as with all Australian species of Corvus, the black feathers have a grey base, and the iris of the adult bird is white. Although the little raven was first named by Gregory Mathews in 1912, it was only in 1967 that there was consensus to separate it from the Australian raven as a distinct species.

children.name: Corvus minor
children.description: A small crow of the Lesser Sunda Islands, one of the smallest Corvus species.

children.name: Corvus moneduloides
children.description: The New Caledonian crow (Corvus moneduloides) is a medium-sized member of the family Corvidae, native to New Caledonia..

children.name: Corvus nasicus
children.description: The Cuban crow (Corvus nasicus) is a crow species native to the northern Caribbean.

children.name: Corvus orru
children.description: The Torresian crow (Corvus orru), also called the Australian crow or Papuan crow, is a passerine bird in the crow family native to the north and west of Australia and nearby islands in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Corvus ossifragus
children.description: The fish crow (Corvus ossifragus) is a species of crow associated with wetland habitats in the eastern and southeastern United States.

children.name: Corvus palmarum
children.description: The Hispaniolan palm crow (Corvus palmarum) is a relatively small corvid endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, which is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

children.name: Corvus philippinus
children.description: The Philippine jungle crow (Corvus philippinus) is a species of crow endemic to the Philippines..

children.name: Corvus propinquus
children.description: A small crow of the Galápagos Islands, with a relatively slender bill.

children.name: Corvus rhipidurus
children.description: The fan-tailed raven (Corvus rhipidurus) is a passerine bird of the crow family native to Eastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula..

children.name: Corvus ruficollis
children.description: The brown-necked raven (Corvus ruficollis) is a larger bird (52–56 cm in length) than the carrion crow though not as large as the common raven..

children.name: Corvus rufigula
children.description: A raven of arid and semi-arid regions from North Africa through the Middle East to Central Asia. Its brownish nape and neck distinguish it from the common raven.

children.name: Corvus sinaloae
children.description: The Sinaloa crow (Corvus sinaloae) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.

children.name: Corvus splendens
children.description: The house crow (Corvus splendens), also known as the Indian, greynecked, Ceylon or Colombo crow, is a common bird of the crow family that is of Asian origin but now found in many parts of the world, where they arrived assisted by shipping.

children.name: Corvus torquatus
children.description: The collared crow (Corvus torquatus), also known as the ring-necked crow or white-collared crow, is a member of the family Corvidae native to China and the north of Vietnam.

children.name: Corvus tristis
children.description: The gray crow, formerly known as the bare-faced crow, is about the same size as the Eurasian carrion crow but has somewhat different proportions and quite atypical feather pigmentation during the juvenile phase for a member of this genus.

children.name: Corvus typicus
children.description: The piping crow (Corvus typicus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.

children.name: Corvus unicolor
children.description: The Banggai crow (Corvus unicolor), known as kuuyak in the Banggai language, is a member of the crow family from Banggai regency in the province of Central Sulawesi in Indonesia.

children.name: Corvus validus
children.description: The long-billed crow (Corvus validus) is a crow that is endemic to the Northern Maluku Islands..

children.name: Corvus violaceus
children.description: The violet crow (Corvus violaceus) is a species of the crow family, Corvidae, native to Seram, an island in Indonesia..

children.name: Corvus woodfordi

They inhabit open woodland, scrub, and bamboo, and are more tolerant of disturbed habitats than most of their relatives.

children.name: Crypsirina temia
children.description: The racket-tailed treepie (Crypsirina temia) is an Asian treepie, a member of the crow family, Corvidae..

children.name: Crypsirina cucullata

children.name: Cyanocitta
children.description: North American blue jays — unmistakable corvids with brilliant blue, white, and black plumage and a conspicuous crest. Among the most familiar birds of North America, they are highly vocal, intelligent, and adaptable, thriving in forests, suburbs, and parks. They are important seed dispersers of oaks and other mast-producing trees, and bold mobbers of raptors and other predators.

children.name: Cyanocitta cristata
children.description: The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.

children.name: Cyanocitta stelleri
children.description: Steller's jay (Cyanocitta stelleri) is a bird native to western North America and the mountains of Central America, closely related to the blue jay (C..

children.name: Cyanocitta cookei
children.description: A brilliant green, blue, and yellow jay of southern Texas, Mexico, and Central America. No other North American bird shares its unique colour palette; its combination of emerald green back, blue crown, black bib, and bright yellow underparts makes it unmistakable at bird feeders in the Lower Rio Grande Valley.

children.name: Cyanocorax
children.description: New World jays — a diverse genus of colourful jays ranging from Mexico to South America, with bold patterns of blue, black, white, and yellow. They inhabit a broad range of forest and woodland habitats and are typically gregarious, noisy birds that move in family parties. Many species are cooperative breeders, and all are intelligent omnivores that exploit a wide variety of food sources.

children.name: Cyanocorax yncas
children.description: The Inca jay (Cyanocorax yncas) is a bird species of the New World jays, which is native to the Andes of South America.

children.description: The curl-crested jay (Cyanocorax cristatellus) is a species of jay native to South America..

children.name: Cyanopica
children.description: Azure-winged magpies — slender, long-tailed corvids with pale underparts and delicate sky-blue wings and tail. Unusually social for corvids, they breed cooperatively with helpers at the nest. They have a striking disjunct distribution: the Iberian Magpie in Portugal and Spain, and the Azure-winged Magpie from the Russian Far East to Japan and China — a distribution once attributed to human introduction but now confirmed as natural.

children.name: Cyanopica cyanus
children.description: The azure-winged magpie (Cyanopica cyanus) is a bird in the crow family..

children.name: Cyanopica cooki

children.name: Dendrocitta
children.description: Treepies — long-tailed corvids of South and Southeast Asian woodlands with warm rufous and grey plumage. Unlike most corvids they are strongly arboreal, racing through canopy and clambering along branches in search of fruit, insects, eggs, and small vertebrates. Their loud, varied calls are a characteristic sound of the Indian subcontinent's forests and gardens.

children.name: Dendrocitta vagabunda
children.description: The rufous treepie (Dendrocitta vagabunda) is a treepie, native to the Indian subcontinent and adjoining parts of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Dendrocitta formosae
children.description: The grey treepie (Dendrocitta formosae), also known as the Himalayan treepie, is an Asian treepie, a medium-sized and long-tailed member of the crow family.

children.name: Dendrocitta leucogastra
children.description: The white-bellied treepie (Dendrocitta leucogastra) is a bird of the crow family endemic to the forests of southern India..

children.name: Dendrocitta occipitalis
children.description: The Sumatran treepie or Sunda treepie (Dendrocitta occipitalis) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.

children.name: Dendrocitta frontalis
children.description: The collared treepie (Dendrocitta frontalis), also known as black-faced treepie or black-browed treepie, is an Asian treepie, a small perching bird of the crow family, Corvidae.

children.name: Dendrocitta cinerascens
children.description: The Bornean treepie (Dendrocitta cinerascens) is a passerine bird belonging to the treepies genus, Dendrocitta, of in the crow family, Corvidae.

children.name: Dendrocitta bayleii

children.name: Garrulus
children.description: The Eurasian Jays — dazzlingly patterned corvids with a sky-blue wing panel, pinkish-brown body, and a raucous, scolding call that serves as a woodland alarm system. Jays are paramount seed dispersers: a single bird buries thousands of acorns each autumn in separate caches up to several kilometres from the source tree, and though it recovers most, enough forgotten caches germinate to drive oak forest regeneration across Europe.

children.name: Garrulus glandarius
children.description: The Eurasian jay, also known simply as the jay without any epithets in the United Kingdom and Ireland, is a species of passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail. The Eurasian jay is a woodland bird that occurs over a vast region from western Europe and north-west Africa to the Indian subcontinent and farther to the eastern seaboard of Asia and down into south-east Asia.

children.name: Garrulus lanceolatus
children.description: The black-headed jay or lanceolated jay (Garrulus lanceolatus) is a species of passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae..

children.name: Garrulus lidthi
children.description: Lidth's jay, also known as the Amami jay, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae native to the Ryukyu Islands, Japan.
children.namedAfter: Baron Georg Heinrich von Lidth de Jeude

children.name: Garrulus bispecularis
children.description: A cryptic species of the western and central Himalayas, formerly considered conspecific with the Eurasian jay but now recognised as distinct based on vocal and genetic evidence.

children.name: Nucifraga
children.description: Nutcrackers — thickset corvids of mountain conifer forests, with a specialised sublingual pouch that can carry up to 90 pine seeds at once. The Spotted Nutcracker is the primary disperser of Swiss stone pine and Arolla pine across the Alps and Carpathians; without it, these trees could not colonise new ground above the existing treeline. The mutualism is so tight that the trees produce seeds too large for most birds other than nutcrackers to handle.

children.name: Nucifraga caryocatactes
children.description: The northern nutcracker (Nucifraga caryocatactes), previously known as the spotted nutcracker and Eurasian nutcracker, is a passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae.

children.name: Nucifraga columbiana
children.description: Clark's nutcracker (Nucifraga columbiana), also known as Clark's crow, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to the mountains of western North America..

children.name: Perisoreus
children.description: Siberian jays — small, fluffy corvids of the taiga, with soft grey-brown plumage and a rusty tail. They are year-round residents of boreal forest and have developed an extraordinary relationship with human hunters, following them through the forest to scavenge scraps — a behaviour that has made them symbols of the northern wilderness in Scandinavian folklore. They cache food year-round and retrieve caches with remarkable spatial memory during winter.

children.name: Perisoreus canadensis
children.description: The Canada jay (Perisoreus canadensis), also known as the grey jay, gray jay, camp robber, moose bird, gorby, or whisky jack, is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae..

children.name: Perisoreus infaustus
children.description: The Siberian jay is a small jay with a widespread distribution within the coniferous forests in North Eurasia. It has grey-brown plumage with a darker brown crown and a paler throat. It is rusty-red in a panel near the wing-bend, on the undertail coverts and on the sides of the tail.

children.name: Perisoreus internigrans
children.description: The Sichuan jay (Perisoreus internigrans) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.

children.name: Pica
children.description: The true magpies — unmistakable black-and-white birds with an extraordinarily long, iridescent green tail. Among the most intelligent animals on Earth, magpies pass the mirror self-recognition test, use tools, hold 'funerals' for dead companions, and cache food while watching for observers, then move the cache if they suspect they have been seen. The Eurasian Magpie has lived alongside humans for millennia and thrives in cities, gardens, and farmland across the entire Palearctic.

children.name: Pica pica
children.description: The Eurasian magpie or common magpie is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent. It is one of several birds in the crow family (corvids) that are designated as magpies, and it belongs to the Holarctic radiation of "monochrome" magpies. In Europe, the term "magpie" is used by English speakers as a synonym for the Eurasian magpie; the only other species of magpie in Europe is the Iberian magpie, which is restricted to the Iberian Peninsula.

children.name: Pica serica
children.description: The Oriental magpie (Pica serica) is a species of magpie found from southeastern Russia to eastern China, Korea, Taiwan, and northern Indochina and Myanmar.

children.name: Pica bottanensis
children.description: The black-rumped magpie (Pica bottanensis) is a species of magpie native to west-central China and Bhutan, and possibly also irregularly in Sikkim in India, and in eastern Nepal..

children.name: Pica hudsonia
children.description: The black-billed magpie (Pica hudsonia), also known as the American magpie, is a bird in the corvid family found in the western half of North America..

children.name: Pica nuttalli
children.description: The yellow-billed magpie (Pica nuttallii), also known as the California magpie, is a bird that is endemic to California's Central Valley and the adjacent chaparral foothills and mountains..

children.name: Pica mauritanica
children.description: The Maghreb magpie (Pica mauritanica) is a species of magpie in the genus Pica found in North Africa from Morocco east to Tunisia, at altitudes from sea level up to 2,300 metres altitude.

children.name: Pica asirensis
children.description: The Asir magpie (Pica asirensis), also known as the Arabian magpie, is a highly endangered species of magpie endemic to Saudi Arabia.

children.name: Podoces
children.description: Ground jays — small to medium corvids of Central Asian deserts and semi-deserts, adapted for a largely terrestrial lifestyle with strong legs, a long decurved bill, and cryptic sandy plumage. They run rapidly across open ground to escape predators rather than taking flight, and forage by probing soil and digging for beetles, lizards, and seeds in some of the driest habitats on Earth.

children.name: Podoces panderi
children.description: The Turkestan ground jay, grey ground jay or Pander's ground-jay (Podoces panderi) is a species of bird in the crow and jay family, Corvidae..

children.name: Podoces biddulphi
children.description: The Xinjiang ground jay (Podoces biddulphi) or Biddulph's ground jay is a species of bird in the family Corvidae..

children.name: Ptilostomus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Piapiac, a slender, long-tailed African corvid with a social lifestyle more reminiscent of mynas than typical crows. The Piapiac is unique among corvids in its association with large mammals, riding on the backs of cattle, camels, and elephants to pick ticks, flies, and disturbed insects from their hides.

children.name: Ptilostomus afer
children.description: The piapiac (Ptilostomus afer) is an African bird in the crow family, and is the only member of the genus Ptilostomus..

children.name: Pyrrhocorax
children.description: Choughs — sleek, all-black corvids with curved bills and buoyant, acrobatic flight that makes them the most aerial members of the family. They inhabit mountain cliffs, sea-cliffs, and upland pastures, probing the soil and dung for invertebrates with their specialised bills. Their high, ringing calls echo off cliff faces throughout their range from Ireland to China.

children.name: Pyrrhocorax pyrrhocorax
children.description: The red-billed chough, Cornish chough or simply chough ( CHUF; Pyrrhocorax pyrrhocorax) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax..

children.name: Pyrrhocorax graculus
children.description: The Alpine chough (; chuf) or yellow-billed chough (Pyrrhocorax graculus) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax.

children.name: Urocissa
children.description: Blue magpies — spectacular corvids of South and East Asian forests, with vivid cobalt-blue plumage, a white-tipped tail sometimes longer than the body, and a red or yellow bill. They are noisy, gregarious birds of forest edges and hillsides, often moving in small parties. Despite their dazzling appearance they behave much like other corvids — omnivorous, opportunistic, and bold.

children.name: Urocissa erythrorhyncha
children.description: The red-billed blue magpie (Urocissa erythroryncha) is a species of bird (magpie) in the crow family, Corvidae..

children.name: Urocissa flavirostris
children.description: The yellow-billed blue-magpie , or gold-billed magpie (Urocissa flavirostris), is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, along with crows and jays..

children.name: Urocissa caerulea
children.description: The Taiwan blue magpie (Urocissa caerulea), also called the Taiwan magpie, Formosan blue magpie ( ), or the "long-tailed mountain lady" ( ; Taiwanese Hokkien: Tn̂g-boé soaⁿ-niû), is a bird species in the crow family.

children.name: Urocissa ornata
children.description: The Sri Lanka blue magpie or Ceylon magpie (Urocissa ornata) is a brightly coloured member of the family Corvidae, found exclusively in Sri Lanka..

children.name: Urocissa whiteheadi
children.description: The white-winged magpie or Hainan magpie is a passerine bird of the crow family, Corvidae. It is unusual among the members of its genus in that it is black and white, lacking the blue plumage other Urocissa magpies have. Thus, it is sometimes placed in its own monotypic genus, Cissopica, though it appears to have sufficient features to remain in the genus Urocissa.

children.name: Zavattariornis
children.description: A monotypic genus known only from a tiny area of southern Ethiopia, containing one of the world's most enigmatic corvids. Stresemann's Bush Crow was unknown to science until 1938 and remains poorly understood, with a bizarrely restricted range that appears to be determined by specific climatic conditions rather than vegetation type.

children.name: Zavattariornis stresemanni
children.description: The Ethiopian bushcrow (Zavattariornis stresemanni), also known as the Stresemann's bushcrow, Abyssinian pie, bush crow, or by its generic name Zavattariornis, is a rather starling-like bird, which is a member of the crow family, Corvidae.

children.description: The grey shrikethrush or grey shrike-thrush (Colluricincla harmonica), formerly commonly known as grey thrush, is a songbird of Australasia.

children.name: Turdus helleri
children.description: The Taita thrush (Turdus helleri), also known as the Taita olive thrush or Heller's ground thrush, is an endangered bird in the thrush family Turdidae, endemic to the Taita Hills in southern Kenya.

children.name: Turdus infuscatus
children.description: The black thrush (Turdus infuscatus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.

children.name: Turdus inquietus
children.description: The restless flycatcher (Myiagra inquieta) or restless myiagra is a passerine bird in the family Monarchidae; it is also known as the razor grinder or scissors grinder because of its distinctive call.

children.name: Turdus lherminieri
children.description: The forest thrush (Turdus lherminieri) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.

children.name: Turdus libonyana
children.description: The Kurrichane thrush (Turdus libonyana) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus ludoviciae
children.description: The Somali thrush (Turdus ludoviciae), also known as the Somali blackbird, is a songbird species in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus maculirostris
children.description: The Ecuadorian thrush (Turdus maculirostris) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus mandarinus
children.description: The Chinese blackbird (Turdus mandarinus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus maximus
children.description: The Tibetan blackbird (Turdus maximus) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus menachensis
children.description: The Yemen thrush (Turdus menachensis) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus merula
children.description: The common blackbird is a species of true thrush. It is also known as the Eurasian blackbird, or simply the blackbird. It breeds in Europe, western Asia, and North Africa, and has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand.

children.name: Turdus migratorius
children.description: The American robin is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family. It is named after the European robin because of its reddish-orange breast, though the two species are not closely related, with the European robin belonging to the Old World flycatcher family. The American robin is widely distributed throughout North America, wintering from southern Canada to central Mexico and along the Pacific coast.

children.name: Turdus mupinensis
children.description: The Chinese thrush (Turdus mupinensis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus murinus
children.description: The pantepui thrush (Turdus murinus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus nigrescens
children.description: The sooty thrush (Turdus nigrescens) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.

children.name: Turdus nudigenis
children.description: The spectacled thrush, bare-eyed thrush, or yellow-eyed thrush (Turdus nudigenis), is a resident breeding bird in the Lesser Antilles and in South America from Colombia and Venezuela south and east to northern Brazil.

children.name: Turdus obscurus
children.description: The eyebrowed thrush (Turdus obscurus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus olivaceus
children.description: The olive thrush (Turdus olivaceus) is, in its range, one of the most common members of the thrush family (Turdidae).

children.name: Turdus pallidus
children.description: The pale thrush (Turdus pallidus) is a passerine bird of the eastern Palearctic belonging to the genus Turdus in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus pectoralis
children.description: The rufous whistler (Pachycephala rufiventris) is a species of whistler found in New Caledonia and Australia.

children.name: Turdus pelios
children.description: The African thrush or West African thrush (Turdus pelios) is a passerine bird in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus philomelos
children.description: The song thrush is a thrush that breeds across the West Palearctic. It has brown upperparts and black-spotted cream or buff underparts and has four recognised subspecies. Its distinctive song, which features repeated musical phrases, has frequently been referenced in poetry.

children.name: Turdus pilaris
children.description: The fieldfare is a member of the thrush family Turdidae. It breeds in woodland and scrub in northern Europe and across the Palearctic. It is strongly migratory, with many northern birds moving south during the winter.

children.name: Turdus plebejus
children.description: The mountain thrush (Turdus plebejus) is species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.

children.name: Turdus roehli
children.description: The Usambara thrush (Turdus roehli), also known as Roehl's thrush or Usambara olive thrush, is a species of thrush found in eastern Africa.

children.name: Turdus rubrocanus
children.description: The chestnut thrush (Turdus rubrocanus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus simillimus
children.description: The Indian blackbird (Turdus simillimus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus smithi
children.description: The Karoo thrush (Turdus smithi), also known as Smith's thrush, is a member of the thrush family in Africa.

children.name: Turdus subalaris
children.description: The blacksmith thrush or eastern slaty thrush (Turdus subalaris) is a passerine bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Turdus torquatus
children.description: The ring ouzel is a mainly European member of the thrush family Turdidae. It is a medium-sized thrush, 23–24 centimetres (9.1–9.4 in) in length and weighing 90–138 grams (3.2–4.9 oz). The male is predominantly black with a conspicuous white crescent across its breast.

children.name: Turdus viscivorus
children.description: The mistle thrush is a bird common to much of Europe, temperate Asia and North Africa. It is a year-round resident in a large part of its range, but northern and eastern populations migrate south for the winter, often in small flocks. It is a large thrush with pale grey-brown upper parts, a greyish-white chin and throat, and black spots on its pale yellow and off-white under parts.

children.name: Zoothera
children.description: Zoothera — a genus of thrushes in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera andromedae
children.description: The Sunda thrush (Zoothera andromedae) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera atrigena
children.description: The Bougainville thrush (Zoothera atrigena) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera dauma
children.description: The scaly thrush (Zoothera dauma) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera lunulata
children.description: The Bassian thrush (Zoothera lunulata), also known as the olive-tailed thrush, is a medium-sized mostly insectivorous thrush found from northern Queensland to southeastern Australia.

children.name: Zoothera major
children.description: The Amami thrush (Zoothera major) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera margaretae
children.description: The Makira thrush (Zoothera margaretae), also known as the San Cristobal thrush, is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Zoothera mollissima
children.description: The alpine thrush (Zoothera mollissima) is a species of bird in the thrush family.

children.name: Zoothera neilgherriensis
children.description: The Nilgiri thrush (Zoothera neilgherriensis) is a member of the thrush family.

children.name: Zoothera salimalii
children.description: The Himalayan thrush or Himalayan forest thrush (Zoothera salimalii) is a species of bird described in 2016 and separated out from the alpine thrush Zoothera mollissima with which they were formerly lumped.

children.name: Zoothera terrestris
children.description: The Bonin thrush (Zoothera terrestris), also known as Kittlitz's thrush or the Bonin Islands thrush, is an extinct species of Asian thrush.

children.name: Zoothera turipavae
children.description: The Guadalcanal thrush (Zoothera turipavae) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

children.name: Fringilla
children.description: The chaffinches — small, brightly-patterned finches and among the commonest birds in Europe. The Common Chaffinch is one of the most abundant wild birds on Earth and a defining presence in virtually every woodland edge, park, and garden on the continent. Their song — a confident, accelerating cascade ending in a curl — is one of the earliest and most persistent sounds of the European spring. Bramblings make one of the most spectacular avian migrations, with tens of millions funnelling through Scandinavia each autumn.

children.name: Fringilla coelebs
children.description: The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch is a common and widespread small passerine Bird – in the finch family. The male is brightly coloured with a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts. The female is more subdued in colouring, but both sexes have two contrasting white wing bars and white sides to the tail.

children.name: Fringilla montifringilla
children.description: The brambling is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It has also been called the cock o' the north and the mountain finch. It is widespread and migratory, often seen in very large flocks.

children.name: Fringilla teydea
children.description: The Tenerife blue chaffinch (Fringilla teydea) is a species of passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.

children.name: Fringilla polatzeki
children.description: The Gran Canaria blue chaffinch (Fringilla polatzeki) is a species of passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae..

children.name: Fringilla alpicolla
children.description: A genetically distinct chaffinch population from the high Alps; proposed as a separate species.

children.name: Fringilla montalbetti
children.description: A recently split species from Corsica and Sardinia; genetically distinct.

children.name: Carduelis
children.description: The European Goldfinch and its relatives — one of the most jewel-like birds of the farmland and garden. The red-white-and-black face and vivid yellow wing-stripe make the Goldfinch instantly recognisable. It specialises in extracting seeds from thistles and teasel heads with its pointed bill — a niche no other small European bird occupies. Goldfinches were once trapped in enormous numbers for the cage-bird trade; legal protection in the 20th century allowed populations to recover substantially.

children.name: Carduelis carduelis
children.description: The European goldfinch, or simply referred to as the goldfinch, is a small passerine bird in the finch family that is native to the Palearctic zone in Europe, northern Africa, and western Asia. It has been introduced to other areas, including Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay and the United States.

children.name: Carduelis citrinella
children.description: The citril finch (Carduelis citrinella), also known as the Alpine citril finch, is a small songbird, a member of the true finch family, Fringillidae.

children.name: Carduelis carduelis caniceps
children.description: The eastern subspecies of the goldfinch; grey head replaces the European red-and-white pattern.

children.name: Carduelis lawrencei
children.description: Lawrence's goldfinch (Spinus lawrencei) is a small songbird of erratic distribution that breeds in California and Baja California and winters in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico..

children.name: Carduelis psaltria
children.description: The lesser goldfinch (Spinus psaltria) is a small finch in the genus Spinus native to the Americas.

children.name: Carduelis notata
children.description: The black-headed siskin (Spinus notatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Carduelis dominicensis
children.description: The Antillean siskin (Spinus dominicensis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Carduelis corsicana
children.description: The Corsican finch (Carduelis corsicana), also known as the Corsican citril finch or Mediterranean citril finch, is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Fringillidae, the "true" finches.

children.name: Carduelis pinus
children.description: The pine siskin (Spinus pinus) is a North American bird in the finch family.

children.name: Carduelis tristis
children.description: The American goldfinch (Spinus tristis) is a small North American bird in the finch family.

children.name: Carduelis xanthogastra
children.description: The yellow-bellied siskin (Spinus xanthogastrus) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Carduelis atrata
children.description: The black siskin (Spinus atratus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Carduelis lawrencii
children.description: A grey-gold finch of California oak savannas with a tinkling song.

children.name: Spinus
children.description: Siskins — small, green-yellow finches of conifers and birches. The Eurasian Siskin is a nomadic bird, wandering across Europe in search of cone and alder crops with restless, twittering flocks. It readily visits garden feeders in winter, particularly for nyjer (thistle) seed. New World siskins include the impressive Pine Siskin and the Lawrence's Goldfinch, illustrating the wide radiation of this lineage across both hemispheres.

children.name: Spinus spinus
children.description: The Eurasian siskin is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is also called the European siskin, common siskin or just siskin. Other (archaic) names include black-headed goldfinch, barley bird and aberdevine.

children.name: Spinus pinus
children.description: The pine siskin (Spinus pinus) is a North American bird in the finch family.

children.name: Spinus tristis
children.description: The American goldfinch (Spinus tristis) is a small North American bird in the finch family.

children.name: Spinus psaltria
children.description: The lesser goldfinch is a small finch in the genus Spinus native to the Americas.

children.name: Spinus magellanicus
children.description: The hooded siskin (Spinus magellanicus) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Spinus cucullatus
children.description: The red siskin (Spinus cucullatus) is a small endangered finch.

children.name: Spinus lawrencei
children.description: Lawrence's goldfinch (Spinus lawrencei) is a small songbird of erratic distribution that breeds in California and Baja California and winters in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico..

children.name: Spinus atratus
children.description: The black siskin (Spinus atratus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Spinus uropygialis
children.description: The yellow-rumped siskin (Spinus uropygialis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus notatus
children.description: The black-headed siskin (Spinus notatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus xanthogastrus
children.description: The yellow-bellied siskin (Spinus xanthogastrus) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus spinescens
children.description: The Andean siskin (Spinus spinescens) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Spinus barbatus
children.description: The black-chinned siskin (Spinus barbatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus crassirostris
children.description: The thick-billed siskin (Spinus crassirostris) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus olivaceus
children.description: The olivaceous siskin (Spinus olivaceus) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Spinus xanthophthalmus
children.description: A striking black-and-yellow siskin from the Peruvian Andes.

children.name: Spinus atriceps
children.description: The black-capped siskin (Spinus atriceps) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus lawrencii
children.description: A small grey-gold finch of California's oak savannas. Its tinkling, canary-like song and nomadic wandering make it a special find for birders.

children.name: Spinus notata
children.description: The black-headed siskin (Spinus notatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus barbata
children.description: The black-chinned siskin (Spinus barbatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias..

children.name: Spinus atrata
children.description: A unique, almost entirely black siskin of the high Peruvian Andes.

children.name: Spinus dominicensis
children.description: The Antillean siskin (Spinus dominicensis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Spinus siemiradzkii
children.description: The saffron siskin (Spinus siemiradzkii) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Spinus spinecens
children.description: A distinctive and well-known species within its range. It inhabits a variety of habitats from lowland forests to mountain highlands, feeding on insects, seeds, and fruits.

children.name: Spinus yarrellii
children.description: The yellow-faced siskin (Spinus yarrellii) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Chloris
children.description: Greenfinches — stout, heavy-billed finches that favour gardens, farmland hedges, and scrub. The European Greenfinch was a common garden bird across much of Europe until a trichomonosis epidemic from 2005 onwards caused population crashes of up to 65% in some countries. Despite this, it remains widespread. Its distinctive descending 'dzeee' call and wheezing song are familiar sounds of suburban gardens. The bill is large and powerful enough to crack large seeds and even olive stones.

children.name: Chloris chloris
children.description: The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.

children.name: Chloris sinica
children.description: The Oriental greenfinch (Chloris sinica), also known as the grey-capped greenfinch, is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae that breeds in broadleaf and conifer woodlands of the East Palearctic.

children.name: Chloris spinoides
children.description: The yellow-breasted greenfinch (Chloris spinoides) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae that is native to the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent..

children.name: Chloris ambigua
children.description: The black-headed greenfinch (Chloris ambigua) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Chloris monguilloti
children.description: The Vietnamese greenfinch (Chloris monguilloti) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Chloris kittlitzi
children.description: The Bonin greenfinch (Chloris kittlitzi), also known as the Ogasawara greenfinch, is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae that is endemic to the Ogasawara Islands of Japan, where it is found on the Bonin Islands and Volcano Islands..

children.name: Chloris ambianus
children.description: A greenfinch from the Philippines; distinctive black chin on the male.

children.name: Chloris monguilii
children.description: A greenfinch of the Himalayan foothills, from Nepal to Myanmar. Its plumage is more yellow than the European species.

children.name: Pyrrhula
children.description: Bullfinches — compact, rounded finches with a stubby, rounded bill and strikingly patterned plumage. The Eurasian Bullfinch male is one of the most vividly coloured small birds in Europe — a claret-red breast, jet black cap, and white rump visible as it flies away. Bullfinches are quiet and often unobtrusive; their plaintive, piping call is the most reliable signal of their presence. They have a specialised tongue and palate for processing seeds by husking them, rather than cracking them.

children.name: Pyrrhula pyrrhula
children.description: The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae. In Anglophone Europe it is known simply as the bullfinch, as it is the original bird to bear the name bullfinch.

children.name: Pyrrhula nipalensis
children.description: The brown bullfinch (Pyrrhula nipalensis) is a species of bird in the true finch family, Fringillidae.

children.name: Pyrrhula aurantiaca
children.description: The orange bullfinch (Pyrrhula aurantiaca) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Pyrrhula erythrocephala
children.description: The red-headed bullfinch (Pyrrhula erythrocephala) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae, found all across the Himalayas and adjacent highlands..

children.name: Pyrrhula erythaca
children.description: The Grey-headed bullfinch (Pyrrhula erythaca), Gray-headed bullfinch, or Beavan's Bullfinch is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Pyrrhula leucogenys
children.description: A Philippine bullfinch; white cheeks and grey-pink body; inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Pyrrhula griseiventris
children.description: The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.

children.name: Pyrrhula leucogenis
children.description: The white-cheeked bullfinch (Pyrrhula leucogenis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Pyrrhula aurantia
children.description: A beautiful orange-breasted bullfinch of the Himalayan region.

children.name: Pyrrhula erythrops
children.description: A small bullfinch of Southeast Asian mountains with white-spotted wing coverts.

children.name: Pyrrhula nigra
children.description: A largely black bullfinch of the Himalayas, with only a hint of rosy colour on the breast.

children.name: Pyrrhula murina
children.description: The Azores bullfinch (Pyrrhula murina), also known as the São Miguel bullfinch, or locally in Portuguese as the priolo, is a threatened passerine bird in the true finch family.

children.name: Loxia
children.description: Crossbills — among the most specialised of all finches, with uniquely crossed bill tips evolved to prize open conifer cones. The crossing of the tips can go either right-over-left or left-over-right; the ratio varies by population. Crossbills are nomadic to an extreme degree, following cone crops across boreal and montane forests. In irruption years they appear far outside their normal range. They are among the very few birds that can breed in any month including mid-winter, timed to peak cone availability.

children.name: Loxia curvirostra
children.description: The red crossbill or common crossbill is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. Crossbills have distinctive mandibles, crossed at the tips, which enable them to extract seeds from conifer cones and other fruits.

children.name: Loxia pytyopsittacus
children.description: The parrot crossbill is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It breeds in pine forests in northern and northeastern Europe.

children.name: Loxia leucoptera
children.description: The two-barred crossbill or white-winged crossbill is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It breeds in the coniferous forests of North America and the Palearctic.

children.name: Loxia scotica
children.description: The Scottish crossbill (Loxia scotica) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.

children.name: Loxia patagonica
children.description: A South American crossbill from the Andes of Chile and Argentina; feeds on Araucaria seeds.

children.name: Loxia ancora
children.description: Endemic to Hispaniola; the only Caribbean crossbill; critically endangered by deforestation.

children.name: Loxia megaplaga
children.description: The Hispaniolan crossbill (Loxia megaplaga) is an Endangered species of passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

children.name: Coccothraustes
children.description: The Hawfinch — the largest finch in Europe, with a massive, pointed, steel-grey bill capable of cracking cherry and olive stones with forces up to 50 kg. Despite its size and striking plumage — orange-brown with a black mask, blue-black wings, and a short white-tipped tail — the Hawfinch is notoriously shy and difficult to observe, keeping to high canopy in mature broadleaf woodland. In winter, small parties gather at hornbeam and wild cherry trees to crack the seeds.

children.name: Coccothraustes coccothraustes
children.description: The hawfinch is a passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only extant species placed in the genus Coccothraustes. Its closest living relatives are the genus Eophona of East Asia, and Hesperiphona of Central and North America.

children.name: Linaria
children.description: Linnets and redpolls — small, streaky brown finches of open country, heathland, and scrub. The Common Linnet's song is one of the most cheerful sounds of a sunny heath or clifftop in spring. The Twite is a montane equivalent, breeding on moorland and coastal salt-marshes. This group has declined markedly across western Europe due to changes in farming practice — specifically the loss of seed-bearing weeds from cultivated fields.

children.name: Linaria cannabina
children.description: The common linnet or Eurasian linnet is a small passerine bird of the finch family, Fringillidae. It derives its common name and the scientific name, Linaria, from its fondness for hemp seeds and flax seeds—flax being the English name of the plant from which linen is made.

children.name: Linaria flavirostris
children.description: The twite is a small brown passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is a partially migratory species that is found in a strongly disjunct distribution in northern Europe, and in Asian mountains from eastern Turkey to Nepal, western China and Mongolia. It mainly feeds on small seeds but occasionally also feeds on insects.

children.name: Linaria yemenensis
children.description: The Yemen linnet (Linaria yemenensis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Acanthis
children.description: Redpolls — small Arctic and boreal finches with a crimson forehead spot and pink-flushed breast in breeding males. Redpoll taxonomy is disputed: some authorities treat Common, Lesser, and Arctic Redpolls as one species with extreme plumage variation, while others recognise three. They are irruptive nomads, appearing in lowland Europe in large numbers in some winters (when birch cone crops fail in Scandinavia) and almost absent in others.

children.name: Acanthis flammea
children.description: The redpoll is a species of small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Acanthis. It breeds in the Arctic and north temperate Holarctic tundra and taiga.

children.name: Acanthis hornemanni
children.description: The redpoll (Acanthis flammea) is a species of small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae..

children.name: Acanthis cabaret
children.description: The redpoll (Acanthis flammea) is a species of small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae..

children.name: Serinus
children.description: Small streaky yellow finches of open and scrubby habitats across Europe and Africa.

children.name: Serinus serinus
children.description: The European serin, or simply the serin, is the smallest species of the family of finches (Fringillidae) and is closely related to the Atlantic canary. Its diet consists mainly of a combination of buds and seeds.

children.name: Serinus canaria
children.description: The Atlantic canary (Serinus canaria), known worldwide simply as the wild canary and also called the island canary, common canary, or canary, is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Serinus in the true finch family, Fringillidae.

children.name: Serinus pusillus
children.description: The red-fronted serin or fire-fronted serin (Serinus pusillus) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae..

children.name: Serinus syriacus
children.description: The Syrian serin (Serinus syriacus) is a brightly coloured small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.

children.name: Serinus alario
children.description: The black-headed canary (Serinus alario) is a species of finch found in Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa..

children.name: Serinus leucopygius
children.description: The white-rumped seedeater (Crithagra leucopygia) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Serinus reichardi
