children.description: The monotonous lark (Mirafra passerina) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa.

children.name: Mirafra collaris
children.description: The collared lark (Amirafra collaris) or collared bushlark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in East Africa.

children.name: Mirafra harterti
children.description: Hartert's Lark is an enigmatic, little-known species from dry scrub in Somalia and adjacent areas of Ethiopia, named after the distinguished German ornithologist Ernst Hartert of the Tring Museum. It is known from very few specimens and its exact taxonomic status has been debated.

children.name: Mirafra naevia
children.description: The sabota lark (Calendulauda sabota) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Mirafra fischeri
children.description: The flappet lark (Amirafra rufocinnamomea) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae that is widespread across Sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Mirafra albicaudatus
children.description: The Somali Bush Lark is a small, pale lark of dry acacia scrub and sandy semi-desert in Somalia and the Ogaden region of Ethiopia. It is one of several endemic or near-endemic lark species found in the Horn of Africa, a hotspot for lark diversity.

children.name: Mirafra torrida
children.description: The Kilimanjaro Lark is a little-known lark of open grasslands at moderate elevations in northern Tanzania and adjacent Kenya, in the zone around Mount Kilimanjaro and the Arusha region. It was previously treated as a subspecies of the Rufous-naped Lark.

children.name: Mirafra levaillantii
children.description: The Natal Lark is a secretive, grassland specialist of moist tall grassland in eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and Swaziland, named in honour of François Le Vaillant, the pioneering French naturalist and ornithologist who explored southern Africa in the late 18th century.

children.name: Mirafra burra
children.description: The red lark (Calendulauda burra), also known as the ferruginous lark or ferruginous sand-lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Mirafra sharpii
children.description: The russet lark (Corypha sharpii), also known as Sharpe's lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in Somalia.

children.name: Chersomanes
children.description: A monotypic genus of robust, long-billed larks of dry scrub and stony plains in southern Africa, close in ecology to the long-billed Certhilauda larks.

children.name: Pinarocorys
children.description: Medium-sized, rather thrush-like African larks of dry open woodland and savanna, less closely associated with bare ground than most larks and more often found in lightly wooded areas.

children.name: Pinarocorys nigricans
children.description: The dusky lark (Pinarocorys nigricans), also known as the dusky bush lark or rufous-rumped bush lark, is a species of migratory lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Ramphocoris
children.description: A monotypic genus of very large-billed larks confined to stony desert and rocky semi-desert across North Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Ammomanes
children.description: Desert finch-larks and desert larks of sandy and rocky deserts from the Sahara across the Arabian Peninsula to South Asia, characterised by plain sandy or rufous plumage and unstreaked underparts that blend with their arid substrates.

children.name: Ammomanes deserti
children.description: The desert lark (Ammomanes deserti) breeds in deserts and semi-deserts from Morocco to western India.

children.name: Ammomanes azizi
children.description: The Saharan Desert Lark is a recently elevated species of central Saharan rock desert, previously treated as a subspecies of Ammomanes deserti. It occupies the rocky regs and hamadas of Algeria, Libya, and Chad, where its pale sandy-grey plumage is an excellent match to the substrate.

children.name: Ammomanopsis
children.description: A monotypic genus closely related to Ammomanes, confined to the gravel plains and stony desert of Namibia and southern Angola. Previously included within Ammomanes, it is now recognised as a separate genus on the basis of molecular and morphological data.

children.name: Chersophilus
children.description: A monotypic genus of Mediterranean and North African semi-deserts, closely allied to Galerida but differing in structure, song, and habitat preferences. Dupont's Lark is highly secretive and more often heard than seen.

children.name: Heteromirafra
children.description: Rare and threatened larks of specialised grassland habitats in eastern Africa and South Africa, closely related to Mirafra but separable by molecular data and highly restricted ranges. Several species have experienced significant population declines.

children.name: Certhilauda
children.description: Long-billed larks of southern African arid and semi-arid zones, with slender, decurved bills used to probe sandy soil and rock crevices for invertebrates. Several species are endemic to the Karoo, Namaqualand, or coastal Namibia.

children.name: Certhilauda barlowi
children.description: The dune lark (Calendulauda erythrochlamys) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Alaudala
children.description: Small, compact short-toed larks split from Calandrella on the basis of molecular phylogenetics, distributed across the Palearctic from the Mediterranean to Central Asia and South Asia. Many members of this genus were previously subsumed within Calandrella brachydactyla or C. rufescens.

children.name: Alaudala heinei
children.description: The Turkestan short-toed lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Ukraine and central Turkey through parts of Central Asia and southern Siberia west to south-central Mongolia and south to southern Afghanistan. This species and the Mediterranean short-toed lark were formerly considered conspecific and called the lesser short-toed lark, but a 2020 study recovered them as distinct species.

children.name: Alaudala rufescens
children.description: The Mediterranean short-toed lark is a small passerine bird found in and around the Mediterranean Basin. It is a common bird with a very wide range from Canary Islands north to the Iberian Peninsula and east throughout North Africa to parts of the Middle East. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Alaudala raytal
children.description: The sand lark (Alaudala raytal) is a small passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae, found in southern Asia.

children.name: Alaudala minor
children.description: The Saharan Short-toed Lark inhabits stony desert, desert margins, and arid scrub across the central and eastern Sahara from Algeria and Libya east to Sudan. It is one of several cryptic short-toed larks of North Africa that were long subsumed within broader species concepts.

children.name: Locustella
children.description: Secretive streaked warblers of dense vegetation producing sustained mechanical insect-like songs. The Grasshopper Warbler can reel continuously for over two minutes. They are among the most difficult European birds to see, creeping through vegetation like small brownish mice.

children.name: Locustella naevia
children.description: The common grasshopper warbler or just grasshopper warbler is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds across much of temperate Europe and the western Palearctic. It is migratory, wintering across northern tropical Africa just south of the Sahara, and also locally in India.

children.name: Locustella fluviatilis
children.description: The river warbler is an Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds in eastern and central Europe and is migratory, wintering in inland southern Africa, from around the Zambezi River south to the vicinity of Pretoria in South Africa.

children.name: Locustella luscinioides
children.description: Savi's warbler is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds in Europe and the western Palearctic. It is migratory, wintering in northern and sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Locustella lanceolata
children.description: The lanceolated warbler is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds from northeast European Russia across the Palearctic to northern Hokkaidō, Japan. It is migratory, wintering in Southeast Asia.

children.name: Locustella alfredi
children.description: The bamboo warbler (Locustella alfredi) or bamboo scrub-warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Megalurus
children.description: Large grassbirds of grasslands and reedbeds in Australasia and South and Southeast Asia. They are long-tailed, streaky brown birds that skulk through dense vegetation and are more often heard than seen.

children.name: Megalurus palustris
children.description: The striated grassbird (Megalurus palustris) is an "Old World warbler" species in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Megalurus gramineus
children.description: The little grassbird (Poodytes gramineus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Cincloramphus
children.description: Songlarks and tawny grassbirds of open grasslands and grassy woodlands in Australia and Southeast Asia. Males of the Australian songlarks perform distinctive aerial song-flights over their territories.

children.name: Cincloramphus cruralis
children.description: The brown songlark (Cincloramphus cruralis), also Australian songlark, is a small passerine bird found throughout much of Australia.

children.name: Cincloramphus mathewsi
children.description: The rufous songlark (Cincloramphus mathewsi) is a species in the family Locustellidae endemic to Australia.

children.name: Cincloramphus timoriensis
children.description: The tawny grassbird (Cincloramphus timoriensis) is a large songbird that is a member of the family Locustellidae commonly found in grassland and reedbed habitats.

children.name: Cincloramphus llaneae
children.description: The Bougainville thicketbird (Cincloramphus llaneae) is a bird species.

children.name: Cincloramphus macrurus
children.description: The Papuan grassbird (Cincloramphus macrurus) is a species of typical grassbird in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Cincloramphus rubiginosus
children.description: The rusty thicketbird (Cincloramphus rubiginosus) is a bird species.

children.name: Cincloramphus whitneyi
children.description: The Santo thicketbird (Cincloramphus whitneyi) is a bird species.

children.name: Schoenicola
children.description: Broadtail warblers of African and Asian grasslands and marshes, characterised by their distinctively broad, graduated tails used in display. They inhabit tall grass and reed habitats.

children.name: Schoenicola striatus
children.description: The bristled grassbird (Schoenicola striatus) is a small passerine bird in the genus Schoenicola.

children.name: Bradypterus
children.description: Bush warblers and scrub warblers of Africa and Asia, inhabiting dense vegetation near water and in montane forests. They are difficult to observe but produce loud, distinctive songs.

children.name: Bradypterus sylvaticus
children.description: The Knysna warbler or Knysna scrub warbler (Bradypterus sylvaticus) is a very shy and cryptic warbler, endemic to the coastal regions of South Africa.

children.name: Bradypterus brunneus
children.description: The brown emutail (Bradypterus brunneus) is an emutail in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Bradypterus seebohmi
children.description: The grey emutail (Bradypterus seebohmi), also known as the Madagascan grassbird or feather-tailed warbler, is an emutail in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Robsonius
children.description: Ground warblers endemic to the Philippines, inhabiting dense undergrowth and forest floor vegetation in montane forests of Luzon and Mindanao. They walk and hop on the ground like thrushes.

children.name: Helopsaltes
children.description: Grass warblers formerly placed in Locustella, separated by genetic evidence and markedly different song structure. They produce varied, flowing warbling songs rather than the mechanical insect-like reeling of true Locustella.

children.name: Helopsaltes pryeri
children.description: The marsh grassbird (Helopsaltes pryeri), also known as the Japanese swamp warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Poodytes
children.description: Small to medium grassbirds of Oceania, inhabiting wetlands, spinifex grasslands, and forest edges. The genus was resurrected following molecular studies that showed Megalurus was polyphyletic.

children.name: Elaphrornis
children.description: A monotypic genus endemic to Sri Lanka, containing the Sri Lanka Bush Warbler. It is sister to the Bradypterus-Megalurus clade but differs in its relatively shorter tail, longer bill, and unmarked plumage.

children.name: Malia
children.description: A monotypic genus endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia. The Malia is a babbler-like bird with olive-green plumage that was long misclassified among the babblers before molecular studies placed it in Locustellidae.

children.name: Malia grata
children.description: The malia (Malia grata) is a medium-sized (approximately 29 cm long) babbler-like passerine.

children.name: Eurocephalus
children.description: Eurocephalus — a genus of shrikes in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius
children.description: The typical shrikes — passerine birds of open country with a hooked bill and a raptor-like hunting style. Shrikes earned the name 'butcher birds' from their habit of impaling prey on thorns and barbed wire as a larder. Despite being songbirds, they hunt insects, small mammals, lizards, and even other birds, striking from exposed perches with surgical precision. The genus is widely distributed across Eurasia, Africa, and North America.

children.name: Lanius excubitor
children.description: The great grey shrike is a large and predatory songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae). It forms a superspecies with its parapatric southern relatives, the Iberian grey shrike, the Chinese grey shrike and the American loggerhead shrike. Males and females are similar in plumage, pearly grey above with a black eye-mask and white underparts.

children.name: Lanius borealis
children.description: The northern shrike (Lanius borealis) is a large songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae) native to North America and Siberia.

children.name: Lanius meridionalis
children.description: The Iberian grey shrike (Lanius meridionalis) is a species of shrike endemic to southwestern Europe.

children.name: Lanius ludovicianus
children.description: The loggerhead shrike (Lanius ludovicianus) is a passerine bird in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius collurio
children.description: The red-backed shrike is a carnivorous passerine bird and member of the shrike family, Laniidae. Its breeding range stretches from Western Europe east to central Russia. It is migratory and winters in the eastern areas of tropical Africa and southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius isabellinus
children.description: The isabelline shrike or Daurian shrike (Lanius isabellinus) is a member of the shrike family (Laniidae).

children.name: Lanius minor
children.description: The lesser grey shrike is a passerine bird in the shrike family Laniidae. It breeds in South and Central Europe and western Asia and migrates to winter quarters in southern Africa in the early autumn, returning in spring. It is a scarce vagrant to western Europe, including Great Britain, usually as a spring or autumn erratic.

children.name: Lanius senator
children.description: The woodchat shrike is a member of the shrike family Laniidae. It can be identified by its red-brown crown and nape. It is mainly insectivorous and favours open wooded areas with scattered trees such as orchards, particularly when there is bare or sandy ground.

children.name: Lanius nubicus
children.description: The masked shrike (Lanius nubicus) is a species of bird in the shrike family, Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius cristatus
children.description: The brown shrike (Lanius cristatus) is a bird in the shrike family that is found mainly in Asia.

children.name: Lanius tigrinus
children.description: The tiger shrike or thick-billed shrike (Lanius tigrinus) is a small passerine bird which belongs to the genus Lanius in the shrike family, Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius somalicus
children.description: thumb|Somali Fiscal The Somali fiscal (Lanius somalicus) is a species of bird in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius collaris
children.description: The southern fiscal or fiscal shrike (Lanius collaris) is a member of the shrike family found through most of southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius anthonyi
children.description: A fiscal shrike endemic to the island of Luzon in the Philippines.

children.name: Lanius validirostris
children.description: The mountain shrike (Lanius validirostris) or grey-capped shrike, is a species of bird in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius taiguanus
children.description: A grey shrike endemic to Taiwan.

children.name: Lanius umbratilis
children.description: A brown shrike endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Lanius malcolmi
children.description: A shrike found in the savannas of eastern Africa.

children.name: Lanius melanopterus
children.description: A black-and-white fiscal found in eastern and southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius dorsalis
children.description: The Taita fiscal or Teita fiscal (Lanius dorsalis) is a member of the shrike family found in east Africa from southeastern South Sudan, southern Ethiopia, and western Somalia to northeastern Tanzania.

children.name: Oriolus
children.description: The typical orioles — brilliantly coloured passerines of the Old World tropics. Males are striking combinations of yellow, black, and crimson; females are more subdued greenish or brownish. Orioles are arboreal, feeding on fruit and insects in the forest canopy. Their fluting, melodic whistles are among the most beautiful bird songs.

children.name: Oriolus auratus
children.description: The African golden oriole (Oriolus auratus), or African oriole, is a member of the oriole family of passerine birds which is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara desert.

children.name: Oriolus boureensis
children.description: An oriole endemic to Buru in the Moluccas.

children.name: Oriolus brachyrynchus
children.description: The western oriole (Oriolus brachyrynchus), or western black-headed oriole, is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae that is native to Africa. The adult upperparts are yellow-olive, and the underparts are yellow in colour.

children.name: Oriolus cruentus
children.description: The Javan oriole (Oriolus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus cupreus
children.description: An oriole with black wings, found in West and Central Africa.

children.name: Oriolus flavocinctus
children.description: The green oriole or Australasian yellow oriole (Oriolus flavocinctus) is an inconspicuous inhabitant of lush tropical vegetation throughout Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Oriolus isabellae
children.description: The Isabela oriole (Oriolus isabellae) is a species of the oriole family endemic to Luzon in the Philippines.

children.name: Oriolus leuconotus
children.description: Oriolus leuconotus (White-backed Oriole) is a african orioles species found in Africa region.

children.name: Oriolus mellianus
children.description: The silver oriole (Oriolus mellianus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus monacha
children.description: The Ethiopian oriole (Oriolus monacha) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus oriolus
children.description: The Eurasian golden oriole, also known as the common golden oriole, is a species of passerine bird and the only Old World oriole breeding in Northern Hemisphere temperate regions. It is a summer migrant in Europe and the Palearctic and spends the winter season in central and southern Africa.

children.name: Oriolus percivali
children.description: The mountain oriole (Oriolus percivali) is a bird species in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus szalayi
children.description: The brown oriole (Oriolus szalayi) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus traillii
children.description: The maroon oriole (Oriolus traillii) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Oriolus viridifuscus
children.description: The Timor oriole (Oriolus melanotis) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Pitohui
children.description: Pitohui — a genus of orioles & figbirds in the family Oriolidae.

children.name: Sphecotheres
children.description: Figbirds — a small genus of three species restricted to Australasia. Unlike typical orioles, figbirds are highly social, gathering in noisy flocks to feed on figs and other fruit. They have a more robust build and a bare patch of facial skin around the eye, giving them a distinctive appearance.

children.name: Sphecotheres vieilloti
children.description: The Australasian figbird (Sphecotheres vieilloti), also known as the green figbird (not to be confused with the Timor figbird), is a conspicuous, medium-sized passerine bird native to a wide range of wooded habitats in northern and eastern Australia, southern New Guinea, and the Kai Islands.

children.name: Anthoscopus
children.description: African penduline tits — tiny, mouse-grey birds of savanna and woodland. They construct the most elaborate nests of any bird: a felted pouch with a false entrance that the bird must push open from below. The entrance is so well-camouflaged that predators cannot find it. Six species across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Anthoscopus flavifrons
children.description: The forest penduline tit is a species of bird in the family Remizidae. It is native to the African tropical rainforest.

children.name: Anthoscopus paradoxus
children.description: Found in northeastern Africa from Ethiopia to Tanzania. Greenish-yellow plumage, unlike the greyer southern species. Inhabits dry acacia woodland and thornbush. Its nest, like other penduline tits, features a cunning false entrance.

children.name: Anthoscopus parvulus
children.description: Yellow penduline tit is a species of bird in the family Remizidae. This small yellow passerine bird is found in semi-arid savanna regions of West Africa.

children.name: Anthoscopus punctifrons
children.description: The Sennar penduline tit is a species of bird in the family Remizidae, the most northerly member of the genus Anthoscopus. It is found in Cameroon, Chad, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, and Sudan. Its natural habitats are dry savanna and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Remiz
children.description: The penduline tits — tiny, acrobatic passerines named for their remarkable hanging nests, woven from plant fibres and spider silk into a pouch suspended from the tip of a thin branch. The Eurasian Penduline Tit weaves an elaborate flask-shaped nest with a false entrance and a hidden side chamber for the eggs. Males build multiple nests and females select the best one.

children.name: Remiz pendulinus
children.description: The Eurasian penduline tit or European penduline tit is a passerine bird of the genus Remiz. It is relatively widespread throughout the western Palearctic. It is migratory in the northern part of its range but resident in the southern part.

children.name: Cinclus
children.description: Dippers — the only aquatic passerines. These stocky, dark-plumaged birds are perfectly adapted for life along fast-flowing streams. They walk and swim underwater, using their wings to 'fly' against the current while searching for insect larvae among the streambed stones. A transparent third eyelid (nictitating membrane) allows them to see underwater. Their loud, ringing song carries above the roar of rapids.

children.name: Cinclus cinclus
children.description: The white-throated dipper (Cinclus cinclus), also known as the European dipper or just dipper, is an aquatic, passerine bird found in Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Cinclus mexicanus
children.description: The American dipper (Cinclus mexicanus), also known as a water ouzel, is a semiaquatic bird species native from North America.

children.name: Cinclus leucocephalus
children.description: The white-capped dipper (Cinclus leucocephalus) is a semiaquatic passerine bird of South America.

children.name: Cinclus pallasii
children.description: thumb|Brown Dipper,Pahalgam, Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir The brown dipper (Cinclus pallasii), also known as Pallas's dipper, Asian dipper or the Asiatic dipper, is an aquatic songbird found in the mountains of the east Palearctic.

children.name: Cinclus schulzi
children.description: The rufous-throated dipper or Argentine dipper (Cinclus schulzii) is a Vulnerable species of semiaquatic songbird of South America.

children.name: Panurus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing only the Bearded Reedling — a small, long-tailed bird of dense reedbeds. Despite the name, it is not a true tit (Paridae) but belongs to its own family. Its 'beard' is actually a striking black moustachial stripe on males. Highly social, they move through reeds in chattering flocks, clinging to vertical stems and acrobatically extracting seeds and insects.

children.name: Panurus biarmicus
children.description: The bearded reedling (Panurus biarmicus) is a small, long-tailed passerine bird found in reed beds near water in the temperate zone of Eurasia.

children.name: Apalis
children.description: Apalis — a genus of cisticolas & allies in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis alticola
children.description: The brown-headed apalis is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Apalis in the family Cisticolidae. Formerly included within the grey apalis but is now commonly considered to be a separate species. It has two subspecies: A.

children.name: Apalis argentea
children.description: The Kungwe apalis is a species in the family Cisticolidae. It was previously considered it to be a subspecies of the buff-throated apalis. It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and Tanzania.

children.name: Apalis bamendae
children.description: The Bamenda apalis (Apalis bamendae) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis binotata
children.description: The lowland masked apalis, also known as the masked apalis, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Tanzania, and Uganda. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Apalis chapini
children.description: Chapin's apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Apalis chariessa
children.description: The white-winged apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Apalis chirindensis
children.description: The Chirinda apalis is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Cisticolidae. This species is endemic to the Eastern Highlands of Zimbabwe and Mozambique. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Apalis cinerea
children.description: The grey apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis flavida
children.description: The yellow-breasted apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis fuscigularis
children.description: The Taita apalis (Apalis fuscigularis) is a bird in the family Cisticolidae that is endemic to the Taita Hills in Kenya.

children.name: Apalis goslingi
children.description: Gosling's apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Gabon. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Apalis jacksoni
children.description: The black-throated apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is native to the Western High Plateau, the Albertine Rift montane forests and the east African montane forests and isolated lowland areas of Cameroon, the DRC and Angola.

children.name: Apalis kaboboensis
children.description: The Kabobo apalis (Apalis kaboboensis) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis karamojae
children.description: The Karamoja apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is endemic to Uganda.

children.name: Apalis lynesi
children.description: The Namuli apalis (Apalis lynesi) is a small African passerine bird belonging to the genus Apalis in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis melanocephala
children.description: The black-headed apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Somalia, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Apalis nigriceps
children.description: The black-capped apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is sparsely distributed throughout the tropical rainforest of Sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Apalis personata
children.description: The mountain masked apalis, also known as the black-faced apalis, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is native to the Albertine Rift montane forests. It was first described in 1902.

children.name: Apalis porphyrolaema
children.description: The chestnut-throated apalis is a species of bird in the cisticola family Cisticolidae. The Kabobo apalis, originally described as a distinct species, is usually treated as a subspecies A. kaboboensis of the chestnut-throated apalis today.

children.name: Apalis ruddi
children.description: Rudd's apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found primarily in Mozambique but also in southern Malawi and adjacent areas of South Africa and Eswatini. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.

children.name: Apalis rufogularis
children.description: The buff-throated apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Angola, Benin, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.

children.name: Apalis sharpii
children.description: Sharpe's apalis is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.

children.name: Apalis thoracica

children.name: Microbates
children.description: Gnatwrens — tiny, stub-tailed wren-like birds of Neotropical forests. Despite their name, they are not wrens but belong to the gnatcatcher family. They skulk in dense undergrowth, constantly flicking their wings and tail, and are more often heard than seen. Their songs are thin, high-pitched trills.

children.name: Microbates collaris
children.description: The collared gnatwren (Microbates collaris) is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae, the gnatcatchers.

children.name: Polioptila
children.description: Gnatcatchers — tiny, active insectivorous birds of the Americas, constantly flicking their long, narrow tails upwards. Their blue-grey upperparts and slender bills give them the appearance of miniature mockingbirds. They are among the most energetic of small passerines, ceaselessly gleaning insects from leaves and twigs.

children.name: Polioptila attenboroughi
children.description: | range_map = Polioptila attenboroughi map.svg.

children.name: Polioptila californica
children.description: The California gnatcatcher (Polioptila californica) is a small, insectivorous bird which frequents dense coastal sage scrub growth.

children.name: Polioptila clemensis
children.description: A gnatcatcher endemic to Cozumel Island, Mexico.

children.name: Polioptila clementsi
children.description: The Iquitos gnatcatcher is a bird in the family Polioptilidae. It was first described in 2005. It is known only from the Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve, west of Iquitos, Peru.

children.name: Polioptila dumicola
children.description: The masked gnatcatcher (Polioptila dumicola) is a small songbird in the family Polioptilidae.

children.name: Polioptila guianensis
children.description: The Guianan gnatcatcher (Polioptila guianensis) is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae.

children.name: Polioptila lembeyei
children.description: The Cuban gnatcatcher is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae, the gnatcatchers. It is endemic to Cuba.

children.name: Polioptila leucogastra
children.description: A gnatcatcher with white belly from Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Polioptila paraensis
children.description: The Para gnatcatcher or Klages's gnatcatcher is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae. It is endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Polioptila plumbea
children.description: The tropical gnatcatcher (Polioptila plumbea) is a small active insectivorous songbird, which is a resident species throughout a large part of northern South America.

children.name: Ramphocaenus
children.description: Long-billed gnatwrens — a monotypic genus of tiny Neotropical birds with an extraordinarily long, fine bill used for extracting insects from crevices. Unlike the closely related Microbates, they have a longer bill and a more upright posture. They inhabit tangled undergrowth and vine tangles in lowland forests.

children.name: Ramphocaenus melanurus
children.description: The trilling gnatwren (Ramphocaenus melanurus), formerly long-billed gnatwren, is a very small bird in the gnatcatcher family.

children.name: Menura
children.description: Lyrebirds — ancient Australian passerines renowned as the world's foremost avian mimics. The male's extraordinary tail, shaped like a Greek lyre when fanned, is the most elaborate of any bird. They can imitate any sound — from other birds' songs to chainsaws, camera shutters, and car alarms — with astonishing fidelity. Despite their superb mimicry, lyrebirds are rarely seen, spending most of their time scratching through forest leaf litter for invertebrates.

children.name: Menura novaehollandiae
children.description: The superb lyrebird (Menura novaehollandiae) is an Australian passerine songbird, one of two species from the family Menuridae, with the other being the much rarer Albert's lyrebird.

children.name: Allenia
children.description: Allenia — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Cinclocerthia
children.description: A genus of mimids endemic to the Lesser Antilles, named for their habit of trembling their wings.

children.name: Cinclocerthia ruficauda
children.description: The brown trembler (Cinclocerthia ruficauda) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae, the mockingbirds and thrashers.

children.name: Cinclocerthia gutturalis
children.description: The grey trembler (Cinclocerthia gutturalis) is a songbird species in the family Mimidae, the mockingbirds and thrashers.

children.name: Dumetella
children.description: The grey catbird — a monotypic genus of medium-sized, slate-grey songbird named for its distinctive mewing call that sounds like a cat. Despite its subdued colouration, it is a gifted mimic, often incorporating the songs of other birds into its own rambling, discontinuous song.

children.name: Dumetella carolinensis
children.description: The gray catbird, also spelled grey catbird, is a medium-sized North American and Central American perching bird of the mimid family. It is the only member of the "catbird" genus Dumetella. Like the black catbird, it is among the basal lineages of the Mimidae, probably a closer relative of the Caribbean thrasher and trembler assemblage than of the mockingbirds and Toxostoma thrashers.

children.name: Margarops
children.description: A monotypic genus of large thrasher found in the Caribbean.

children.name: Melanoptila
children.description: Melanoptila — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Melanoptila glabrirostris
children.description: The black catbird is a songbird species in the monotypic genus Melanoptila, part of the family Mimidae. At 19–20.5 cm (7.5–8.1 in) in length and 31.6–42 g (1.11–1.48 oz) in mass, it is the smallest of the mimids. Sexes appear similar, with glossy black plumage, black legs and bill, and dark brownish eyes.

children.name: Melanotis
children.description: A genus of striking blue-grey mockingbirds found in Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Melanotis caerulescens
children.description: The blue mockingbird (Melanotis caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus
children.description: Typical mockingbirds — medium-sized, long-tailed passerines with grey upperparts and pale underparts. Renowned for their extraordinary vocal abilities, mockingbirds can imitate dozens of other bird species, as well as frogs, dogs, and mechanical sounds. They are among the most accomplished avian mimics in the New World. Found from the United States to South America.

children.name: Mimus gilvus
children.description: The tropical mockingbird (Mimus gilvus) is a resident breeding bird from southern Mexico to northern and eastern South America and in the Lesser Antilles and other Caribbean islands.

children.name: Mimus gundlachii
children.description: The Bahama mockingbird is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. It is found in the Bahamas, Cuba, Jamaica and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and is a vagrant to Florida.

children.name: Mimus patagonicus
children.description: The Patagonian mockingbird (Mimus patagonicus) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus polyglottos
children.description: The northern mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos) is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus thenca
children.description: The Chilean mockingbird (Mimus thenca), locally known as tenca, is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus trifasciatus
children.description: The Floreana mockingbird or the Charles Island mockingbird, is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. It was endemic to Floreana, one of the Galápagos Islands, but now is found only on two nearby islets, Campeón and Gardner-near-Floreana. The Floreana mockingbird is also known as Darwin's mockingbird, as it was the arguable inspiration for Charles Darwin's work on the origins of species; he noticed distinct differences between them and previous species he had encountered and consequently established the existence of other variants on neighboring islands.

children.name: Oreoscoptes
children.description: Oreoscoptes — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Oreoscoptes montanus
children.description: The sage thrasher is a medium-sized passerine bird in the family Mimidae. It is the only species in the genus Oreoscoptes and the smallest of the thrashers. It is found in the regions of western North America, breeding from the Great Basin to southern British Columbia, and migrates south to southern United States and northern Mexico for winter.

children.name: Ramphocinclus
children.description: Ramphocinclus — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Ramphocinclus brachyurus
children.description: The Martinique thrasher is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. Semper and Sclater (1872) describe the white-breasted thrasher as an "inquisitive and noisy bird" that would often "keep up a constant warning chatter, and throw itself about in all sorts of contortions" when being disturbed. It is endemic to Martinique.

children.name: Toxostoma
children.description: Thrashers — long-tailed, long-billed songbirds of dry, open country in North America. They use their curved bills to sweep through leaf litter, searching for insects. Their skulking habits often make them harder to see than to hear — their songs are long, complex, and melodious, often given from exposed perches.

children.name: Toxostoma cinereum
children.description: The gray thrasher (Toxostoma cinereum) is a medium-sized passerine bird belonging to the family Mimidae.

children.name: Toxostoma crissale
children.description: The crissal thrasher (Toxostoma crissale) is a large thrasher found in the Southwestern United States (western Texas, southern New Mexico, southern Arizona, southeastern California, extreme southern Nevada, and extreme southwestern Utah) to central Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma guttatum
children.description: The Cozumel thrasher (Toxostoma guttatum) is a bird from the mockingbird family (Mimidae), which is endemic to the island of Cozumel off the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma leuconotum
children.description: A pale grey-brown thrasher of desert scrub in southwestern US and Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma ocellatum
children.description: The ocellated thrasher (Toxostoma ocellatum) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Toxostoma redivivum
children.description: The California thrasher (Toxostoma redivivum) is a large member of family Mimidae found primarily in chaparral habitat in California in the United States and Baja California in Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma rufum
children.description: The brown thrasher (Toxostoma rufum), sometimes erroneously called the brown thrush or fox-coloured thrush, is a bird in the family Mimidae, which also includes the New World catbirds and mockingbirds.

children.name: Anthreptes
children.description: Anthreptes — a genus of sunbirds in the family Nectariniidae.

children.name: Anthreptes anchietae
children.description: Anchieta's sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in Angola, the DRC, Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zambia, and is named after José Alberto de Oliveira Anchieta.

children.name: Anthreptes aurantius
children.description: The violet-tailed sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found near water in forest, scrub and mangrove in the Central African countries of Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Gabon. It is part of the violet-backed sunbird superspecies.

children.name: Anthreptes gabonicus
children.description: The mangrove sunbird or mouse-brown sunbird, is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. Its range covers areas near the Gulf of Guinea, from Senegal to northwestern Angola.

children.name: Anthreptes griseigularis
children.description: The grey-throated sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in a wide range of semi-open wooded habitats in the northern and eastern part of the Philippines. It is often considered a subspecies of the brown-throated sunbird, but the two differ consistently in measurements and plumage, and there is no evidence of intergradation between them.

children.name: Anthreptes longuemarei
children.description: The western violet-backed sunbird or Longuemare's sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is the most widely ranging species in the violet-backed sunbird superspecies, ranging throughout a large part of tropical mainland sub-Saharan Africa not inhabited by other members of the superspecies. It is mainly found in regions with mesic woodland.

children.name: Anthreptes malacensis
children.description: The brown-throated sunbird, also known as the plain-throated sunbird, is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in a wide range of semi-open habitats in south-east Asia, ranging from Myanmar to the Lesser Sundas and west Philippines. The grey-throated sunbird found in the remaining part of the Philippines is often considered a subspecies of the brown-throated sunbird, but the two differ consistently in measurements and plumage, and there is no evidence of intergradation between them.

children.name: Anthreptes neglectus
children.description: The Uluguru violet-backed sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. The bird is small with a short bill. The male is an iridescent upper body while the female has a brown upperbody.

children.name: Anthreptes orientalis
children.description: The eastern violet-backed sunbird, also known as the Kenya violet-backed sunbird, is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in arid savanna of East Africa, ranging from Djibouti in north to Tanzania in south. It is part of the violet-backed sunbird superspecies.

children.name: Anthreptes rectirostris
children.description: The yellow-chinned sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in West Africa, namely Sierra Leone to Ghana. The grey-chinned sunbird was formerly grouped with this species.

children.name: Anthreptes reichenowi
children.description: The plain-backed sunbird, also known as blue-throated sunbird is a sunbird. It is found in Southeast Asia and is not considered a threatened species by the IUCN.

children.name: Ixos nicobariensis

children.name: Ixos virescens

children.description: The common bulbul is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is widespread throughout most of Africa except for the very arid areas, and has recently begun breeding in southernmost Spain. Ten subspecies are recognised based on the geographical variation in plumage.

children.name: Pycnonotus dodsoni

children.name: Pycnonotus hualon
children.description: The bare-faced bulbul is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It was newly described from central Laos in 2009. It is one of the very few Asian songbirds with a bald (featherless) face and is the first new species of bulbul to be described from Asia in almost a century.

children.name: Pycnonotus jocosus
children.description: The red-whiskered bulbul, or crested bulbul, is a passerine bird native to Asia. It is a member of the bulbul family. It is a resident frugivore found mainly in tropical Asia.

children.name: Pycnonotus leucogenys

children.name: Pycnonotus montis

children.name: Pycnonotus nigricans

children.name: Pycnonotus priocephalus
children.description: The grey-headed bulbul is a member of the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is endemic to the Western Ghats in south-western India, and found from Goa south to Tamil Nadu at altitudes up to 1200m. It is found in dense reeds or thickets mainly near rivers and swampy areas inside forests.

children.name: Pycnonotus sinensis
children.description: The light-vented bulbul, also called the Chinese bulbul, is a species of bird in the bulbul family found in Asia. A common species of songbird that favors lightly wooded habitats, it can frequently be seen in towns, suburbs and urban parks within its range.

children.name: Taeniopygia
children.description: The zebra finches — a small genus of Australasian estrildids known for their distinctively patterned plumage and remarkable adaptability to arid environments. The Zebra Finch is one of the most studied songbirds in laboratory research, particularly in neurobiology, learning, and vocal communication. They are social, gregarious birds that form enormous flocks in suitable habitat.

children.name: Padda
children.description: The Java sparrows — a small genus of stocky, large-billed estrildids native to islands of Southeast Asia. They are notable for their thick, conical bills adapted for husking rice and other grains. The Java Sparrow has been a popular cage bird in Asia for centuries, which has led to extensive introductions across the tropics. They are highly social and often roost in large communal groups.

children.name: Erythrura
children.description: The parrotfinches — a genus of brightly coloured estrildids with green, red, and blue plumage that give them a parrot-like appearance. They are found from Southeast Asia to the Pacific islands, with the highest diversity in New Guinea. Their stout, curved bills are adapted for feeding on grass seeds, figs, and bamboo seeds. Many species are prized in aviculture.

children.name: Erythrura gouldiae
children.description: The Gouldian finch (Chloebia gouldiae), also known as the Gould's finch or the rainbow finch, is a colourful passerine bird that is native to Australia.

children.name: Erythrura pealii
children.description: The Fiji parrotfinch (Erythrura pealii) is a species of estrildid finch endemic to Fiji that was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the red-headed parrotfinch.

children.name: Erythrura tricolor
children.description: The tricolored parrotfinch (Erythrura tricolor) is a species of estrildid finch found in Timor and the southern Moluccas.

children.name: Erythrura papuana
children.description: The Papuan parrotfinch (Erythrura papuana) is a common species of estrildid finch found in New Guinea.

children.name: Erythrura regia
children.description: The royal parrotfinch (Erythrura regia) is a species of estrildid finch endemic to Vanuatu in the South Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Lonchura
children.description: The munias and mannikins — a large genus of seed-eating estrildids distributed across Africa, Asia, and Australasia. They are stout, typically brown or black seedeaters with conical bills, often with contrasting white or dark heads and bellies. Highly gregarious, they form noisy flocks in grasslands and rice paddies. Several species have been domesticated and are popular cage birds, including the Society Finch.

children.name: Lonchura domestica
children.description: A domesticated finch derived from the White-rumped Munia through centuries of selection in Japan and China. It is not found in the wild but exists only in captivity, where it is known for its gregarious, non-aggressive temperament and free-breeding habits. Its varied colour morphs include chocolate, pied, and fawn. It is often used as a foster parent for other estrildids in aviculture.

children.name: Lonchura malacca
children.description: The tricoloured munia (Lonchura malacca) is an estrildid finch, native to Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and southern China.

children.name: Lonchura stygia
children.description: The black mannikin (Lonchura stygia) or black munia, is a species of estrildid finch found in New Guinea, from Mandum (Papua, formerly known as Irian Jaya, Indonesia) to Lake Daviumbu, Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Lonchura spectabilis
children.description: The hooded mannikin or hooded munia (Lonchura spectabilis), also known as the New Britain mannikin or Sclater's mannikin, is a species of estrildid finch found in New Britain and New Guinea.

children.name: Lonchura mela
children.description: A small munia with black wings, brown body, and white belly. It is found in grasslands of the Lesser Sunda Islands.

children.name: Lonchura pectoralis
children.description: A munia with a black face and bib, white breast with dark scaling, brown back, and black belly. It is found in dry grasslands of northern Australia.

children.name: Amadina
children.description: The cut-throat and related finches — a small genus of African estrildids with stout cones and distinctive throat patterns. The Cut-throat Finch is named for the male's vivid red throat band that resembles a wound. These are birds of dry savannas and scrublands, often gathering at waterholes in large numbers. They build untidy grass nests in trees or bushes, often reusing old weaver nests.

children.name: Amandava
children.description: The avadavats — a small genus of brilliantly plumaged Asian estrildids with striking red breeding plumage in males. They are among the most colourful small passerines in Asia, with the male Red Avadavat covered in tiny white spots set against a red background. They frequent tall grasslands and wetlands, building domed grass nests with a side entrance.

children.name: Amandava amandava
children.description: The red avadavat (Amandava amandava), red munia or strawberry finch, is a sparrow-sized bird of the family Estrildidae.

children.name: Amandava formosa
children.description: The green avadavat or green munia (Amandava formosa) is a species of Estrildid finch with green and yellow on the body, a bright red bill and black "zebra stripes" on the flanks.

children.name: Uraeginthus
children.description: The blue waxbills — a small genus of strikingly coloured African estrildids with brilliant blue faces, throats, and underparts. These delicate, fine-billed seedeaters are among the most beautiful African finches, occurring across savanna and woodland habitats. They are active, cheerful birds, often seen in pairs or small flocks at the edges of woodlands and in gardens.

children.name: Uraeginthus angolensis
children.description: The blue waxbill (Uraeginthus angolensis), also called southern blue waxbill, blue-breasted waxbill, southern cordon-bleu, blue-cheeked cordon-bleu, blue-breasted cordon-bleu and Angola cordon-bleu, is a common species of estrildid finch found in Southern Africa.

children.name: Estrilda
children.description: The typical waxbills — a large genus of small, delicately proportioned estrildids found across Africa. They are named for the waxy red colouration of their bills, which resembles sealing wax. These active, social finches are predominantly fawn, grey, and brown with fine barring, and many show a distinctive red or black eye-stripe. They feed on grass seeds and small insects, often in large flocks at water sources.

children.name: Estrilda astrild
children.description: The common waxbill, also known as the St Helena waxbill, is a small passerine bird belonging to the estrildid finch family. It is native to sub-Saharan Africa but has been introduced to many other regions of the world and now has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 10,000,000 km2. It is popular and easy to keep in captivity.

children.name: Estrilda poliopareia
children.description: The Anambra waxbill (Estrilda poliopareia) is a species of estrildid finch found in wetter land of southern Nigeria and Benin.

children.name: Brunhilda
children.description: A small genus of African waxbills with distinctive black, white, and red facial patterns. They were formerly included in Estrilda but are distinguished by their heavier bills and striking black-and-red facial masks. They inhabit dry savanna and thorn scrub across eastern and southern Africa.

children.name: Spermophaga
children.description: The bluebills — a small genus of large, robust estrildids with heavy blue-grey bills adapted for cracking hard seeds. They are found in forests and dense thickets across tropical Africa. Males are strikingly coloured with red, black, and white plumage, while females are duller. They are shy, retiring birds that forage on the forest floor.

children.name: Spermophaga haematina
children.description: The western bluebill (Spermophaga haematina) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Africa.

children.name: Mandingoa
children.description: A monotypic genus of African estrildid containing the Green Twinspot. It is a beautifully coloured finch of lowland and montane forests, with a glittering spotted breast that gives it its name. Its iridescent green spots are unique among African waxbills.

children.name: Lagonosticta
children.description: The firefinches — a genus of small, beautifully coloured African estrildids named for the brilliant crimson and pink plumage of the males. They are among the most vividly coloured small birds in Africa, with females being duller brownish versions. They inhabit savanna, scrub, and forest edges, often near water, and build domed grass nests with a side entrance.

children.name: Lagonosticta rubricata
children.description: The African firefinch (Lagonosticta rubricata), also called the blue-billed firefinch, is a common species of estrildid finch found in many parts of Africa.

children.name: Lagonosticta nitidula
children.description: The brown firefinch (Lagonosticta nitidula) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Southern Africa.

children.name: Lagonosticta landanae
