They are active insectivores that forage in the forest understorey, catching insects in short sallies from a perch. Their plumage is a combination of yellow, black, and white, making them distinctive among New Guinea's rich avifauna.

children.name: Artamella
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing the White-headed Vanga. It has a striking white head contrasting with black wings and tail, and a relatively slender, straight bill adapted for gleaning insects from foliage. It is a social species often seen in small groups.

children.name: Calicalicus
children.description: A genus of small, sexually dimorphic vangas endemic to Madagascar, with males sporting bright red or chestnut patches on the wings and tail. They are among the smallest members of the vanga family and are active, acrobatic foragers in the forest canopy. Their short, stout bills are adapted for gleaning insects from foliage rather than the specialised foraging of other vangas.

children.name: Calicalicus rufocarpalis
children.description: The red-shouldered vanga is a member of the vanga family endemic to south-west Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius
children.description: A monotypic genus of strikingly coloured vanga with brilliant azure-blue upperparts that are unique among Malagasy passerines. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is more of a canopy insectivore than other vangas. Its distribution extends beyond Madagascar to the Comoros Islands, unusual for the family, which is otherwise entirely restricted to Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius comorensis
children.description: The Comoros blue vanga or Comoro blue vanga is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is found in the Comoros, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Euryceros
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the extraordinary Helmet Vanga, one of the most distinctive birds in Madagascar. It has a massive, deep, laterally compressed bill that is a vivid blue-grey and forms a prominent casque on the forehead. This remarkable adaptation is used to crush large insects and other prey. It is a large, robust vanga of eastern rainforests.

children.name: Euryceros prevostii
children.description: The helmet vanga (Euryceros prevostii) is a distinctive-looking bird of the vanga family, Vangidae, and is classified in its own genus, Euryceros.

children.name: Falculea
children.description: A monotypic vanga genus containing the Sickle-billed Vanga, which possesses the most extreme bill morphology in the family: a long, slender, strongly decurved bill resembling a sickle. This highly specialised tool is used to probe deep into tree crevices and bark furrows for large insects. Endemic to Madagascar, it is the largest species in the vanga family.

children.name: Hypositta
children.description: A monotypic genus of small vanga containing the Nuthatch Vanga, which convergently resembles a nuthatch in both morphology and behaviour. It has a short, straight bill and strong feet, and is unique among vangas for its tree-creeping foraging style, spiralling up trunks and branches in search of insects. Endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Hypositta corallirostris
children.description: The nuthatch vanga (Hypositta corallirostris), also known as the coral-billed nuthatch-vanga and formerly as the coral-billed nuthatch, is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Leptopterus
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing the Chabert Vanga, a small, pale-eyed species endemic to Madagascar. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is an active canopy insectivore, often joining mixed-species flocks. Its pale blue-grey plumage makes it one of the more subtly coloured vangas.

children.name: Leptopterus chabert
children.description: thumb|Chabert vanga near Toliara, SW Madagascar The chabert vanga (Leptopterus chabert), also erroneously called "Chabert's vanga", is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Mystacornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of terrestrial vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing Crossley's Vanga. It has a long, slender, slightly decurved bill and strong legs, adapted for a ground-foraging lifestyle in the leaf litter of the forest floor. It is one of the most secretive and poorly known members of the vanga family.

children.name: Newtonia
children.description: A genus of small, warbler-like vangas endemic to Madagascar, with relatively slender, pointed bills and active foraging styles. They were traditionally placed in the Old World warbler family Sylviidae before molecular studies revealed their true affinities within the vanga family. They are insectivorous birds of forest and scrub habitats.

children.name: Newtonia amphichroa
children.description: The dark newtonia (Newtonia amphichroa) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Newtonia brunneicauda
children.description: The common newtonia (Newtonia brunneicauda) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Newtonia larvata
children.description: A masked newtonia of the Comoro Islands.

children.name: Newtonia lavarambo
children.description: The dark newtonia is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to northeastern Madagascar. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Newtonia micrura
children.description: A very small vanga with short tail, found in dry forests of western Madagascar.

children.name: Oriolia
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing Bernier's Vanga, a striking black-and-white species endemic to Madagascar. It has a stout, slightly hooked bill and a distinctive white wing patch. It is a forest-dwelling insectivore that forages actively in the canopy, often in mixed-species flocks.

children.name: Oryzoborus
children.description: A genus of seed-eating birds formerly placed in the tanager family.

children.name: Pseudobias
children.description: Pseudobias — a genus in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Pseudobias wardi
children.description: Ward's vanga, also known as Ward's flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Pseudobias. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus
children.description: Small vangas formerly placed in the thrush family.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus
children.description: Small vangas from Madagascar.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus
children.description: Small vangas from Madagascar.

children.name: Schetba
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing the Rufous Vanga, a medium-sized, sexually dimorphic species endemic to Madagascar. The male is strikingly coloured with a rufous back and head, while the female is more subdued. It has a relatively stout bill and forages actively in the forest mid-storey.

children.name: Schetba rufa
children.description: The rufous vanga (Schetba rufa) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Tephrodornis
children.description: Tephrodornis — a genus in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Tephrodornis affinis
children.description: The Sri Lanka woodshrike is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is found on Sri Lanka. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the common woodshrike.

children.name: Tephrodornis pondicerianus
children.description: The common woodshrike is a species of bird found in Asia. It is now usually considered a member of the family Vangidae. It is small and ashy brown with a dark cheek patch and a broad white brow.

children.name: Tephrodornis sylvicola
children.description: The Malabar woodshrike is a species of bird usually placed in the family Vangidae. It is found in western India. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the large woodshrike.

children.name: Tephrodornis virgatus
children.description: The large woodshrike is found in south-eastern Asia, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo. Its natural habitats are temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Tylas
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga with striking black-and-white plumage.

children.name: Tylas albicollis
children.description: A striking black-and-white vanga from eastern Madagascar.

children.name: Tylas
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga.

children.name: Tylas albicollis
children.description: A striking black-and-white vanga from eastern Madagascar.

children.name: Tylas
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga.

children.name: Tylas albicollis
children.description: A striking black-and-white vanga from eastern Madagascar.

children.name: Tylas eduardi
children.description: The tylas vanga is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Tylas. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Vanga
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Hook-billed Vanga, the namesake of the vanga family, endemic to Madagascar. It has a thick, strongly hooked bill that is distinctly crossed at the tip, an adaptation for extracting prey from tree crevices. It is a medium-sized, boldly patterned bird with a black-and-white plumage that makes it easily identifiable in the Malagasy forests.

children.name: Xenopirostris
children.description: A genus of three medium-sized vangas endemic to Madagascar, characterised by a laterally compressed, blade-like bill that is unique among birds. This remarkable adaptation is used to peel bark and pry into crevices in search of prey. They inhabit dry forests and are among the most specialised foragers in the vanga family.

children.name: Pityriasis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Bornean Bristlehead, one of the most unusual and enigmatic passerines in Southeast Asia. It is a large, stocky forest bird with a distinctive bald, bristly red head that gives the family its common name. The species is so distinctive that was historically placed in its own family entirely, and its closest relatives remain a subject of taxonomic debate.

children.name: Pityriasis gymnocephala
children.description: The Bornean bristlehead (Pityriasis gymnocephala), also variously known as the bristled shrike, bald-headed crow or the bald-headed wood-shrike, is the only member of the passerine family Pityriasidae and genus Pityriasis.

children.name: Artamus
children.description: The woodswallows — a genus of highly social, aerial insectivores with a superficial resemblance to swallows, for which they are named. They have broad, triangular wings, short tails, and stout, finch-like bills adapted for catching insects on the wing. They are among the most gregarious of all Australasian passerines, often packing tightly together on exposed branches in large, noisy flocks.

children.name: Artamus cyanopterus
children.description: The dusky woodswallow (Artamus cyanopterus) The global population of the species has as yet not been formally confirmed, but it has been officially rated in the range of 'Least Concern', according to the BirdLife International in 2004.

children.name: Artamus flaviventer
children.description: A woodswallow with yellow vent from the Moluccas and New Guinea.

children.name: Artamus fuscus
children.description: The ashy woodswallow, sometimes also called the ashy swallow-shrike, is a woodswallow which is found in south Asia. Like other woodswallows, it has a short curved bill, a short square tail and long wings. It is usually seen perched in groups, high on powerlines, tall bare trees and most often in areas with a predominance of tall palm trees.

children.name: Artamus leucoryn
children.description: The white-breasted woodswallow is a medium-sized passerine bird which breeds from the Andaman Islands east through Indonesia and northern Australia. The name "woodswallow" is a misnomer as they are not closely related to true swallows. Instead, they belong to the family Artamidae, which also includes butcherbirds, currawongs and the Australian magpie.

children.name: Artamus maximus
children.description: The great woodswallow (Artamus maximus), also known as the greater woodswallow, giant woodswallow or New Guinea woodswallow, is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Artamus melanops
children.description: A woodswallow with black face from the Lesser Sunda Islands.

children.name: Artamus mentalis
children.description: The Fiji woodswallow is a species of woodswallow in the family Artamidae. It is endemic to most of the islands of Fiji, although it is absent from Kadavu Archipelago and the Lau Archipelago. The species was once considered a race of the white-breasted woodswallow, which breeds from Australia, New Caledonia and Vanuatu through to Borneo and the Philippines.

children.name: Artamus minor
children.description: The little woodswallow (Artamus minor), is a bird patchily distributed over much of mainland Australia, avoiding only the driest deserts and the area within about 300 kilometres of the southern coastline, and showing a preference for rugged terrain around inland ranges.

children.name: Artamus personatus
children.description: Masked woodswallow (Artamus personatus) is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus
children.description: The butcherbirds — a genus of medium-sized, stocky passerines with strongly hooked bills bearing a distinct tooth-like notch, an adaptation for their predatory feeding habits. They earned their common name from their habit of impaling prey on thorns or wedging it in tree forks as a 'larder'. They are accomplished songsters with rich, flute-like calls.

children.name: Cracticus nigrogularis
children.description: The pied butcherbird (Cracticus nigrogularis) is a songbird native to Australia.

children.name: Cracticus torquatus
children.description: The grey butcherbird (Cracticus torquatus) is a widely distributed species endemic to Australia.

children.name: Cracticus quoyi
children.description: The black butcherbird (Melloria quoyi) is a species of butcherbird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus cassicus
children.description: The hooded butcherbird (Cracticus cassicus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus louisiadensis
children.description: The Tagula butcherbird (Cracticus louisiadensis) is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Gymnorhina
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Australian Magpie, one of Australia's most iconic and familiar birds. Despite its name, it is not closely related to the Northern Hemisphere magpies but belongs to the butcherbird family. It is a large, boldly patterned black-and-white bird with a famously complex and melodious carolling song, and is renowned for its territorial swooping during breeding season.

children.name: Gymnorhina tibicen
children.description: thumb|Adult with juvenile [[Taveuni, Fiji]].

children.name: Melloria
children.description: Melloria — a genus of woodswallows & butcherbirds in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Melloria quoyi
children.description: The black butcherbird is a species of butcherbird in the family Artamidae. It is found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.

children.name: Rhagologus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Mottled Berryhunter, a recently recognised family-level lineage endemic to the montane forests of New Guinea. It was historically placed with the whistlers or woodswallows but molecular studies revealed it is sufficiently distinct to warrant its own family. It is a medium-sized passerine with a stout, thrush-like build and a heavy bill adapted for feeding on fruit and large insects.

children.name: Rhagologus leucostigma
children.description: The mottled berryhunter or mottled whistler (Rhagologus leucostigma) is a species of bird whose relationships are unclear but is most likely related to the woodswallows, boatbills and butcherbirds.

children.name: Aegithina
children.description: A genus of small, active passerines found across South and Southeast Asia, with a slender build, short wings, and a habit of constant, restless movement through the canopy. Males are more brightly coloured than females, with bold black-and-yellow or green-and-yellow plumage patterns. They are highly vocal, with complex, whistled songs that are delivered in an energetic, undulating flight display.

children.name: Aegithina tiphia
children.description: , Bangladesh]] The common iora (Aegithina tiphia) is a small passerine bird found across the tropical Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, with populations showing plumage variations, some of which are designated as subspecies.

children.name: Aegithina viridissima
children.description: The green iora (Aegithina viridissima) is a species of bird in the family Aegithinidae.

children.name: Aegithina lafresnayei
children.description: The great iora (Aegithina lafresnayei) is a species of bird in the family Aegithinidae.

children.name: Coracina
children.description: The larger cuckooshrikes — a widespread genus of medium to large passerines found from Africa through Asia to Australasia, with grey, black, and white plumage and stout, slightly hooked bills. Despite their name, they are neither cuckoos nor shrikes, but an independent family of arboreal insectivores. Many species are highly vocal with loud, fluty, far-carrying calls.

children.name: Coracina macei
children.description: The Indian cuckooshrike (Coracina macei) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae that is found on the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Coracina bicolor
children.description: The pied cuckooshrike (Coracina bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina larvata
children.description: The Sunda cuckooshrike (Coracina larvata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina longicauda
children.description: The hooded cuckooshrike (Coracina longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina lineata
children.description: The barred cuckooshrike (Coracina lineata), also called the yellow-eyed cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina schistacea
children.description: The slaty cuckooshrike (Coracina schistacea) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina atriceps
children.description: The Moluccan cuckooshrike (Coracina atriceps) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina caesia
children.description: The grey cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris caesius) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina cinerea
children.description: The Madagascar cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris cinereus), also known as the ashy cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina coerulescens
children.description: The blackish cuckooshrike (Edolisoma coerulescens) or the blackish cicadabird or Luzon graybird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina personata
children.description: The Wallacean cuckooshrike (Coracina personata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina fortis
children.description: The Buru cuckooshrike (Coracina fortis) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina temminckii
children.description: The cerulean cuckooshrike (Coracina temminckii) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina dobsoni
children.description: The Andaman cuckooshrike (Coracina dobsoni) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina nebulosa
children.description: A small, green and yellow bird with intricate markings, known for its unique song that mimics other local species.

children.name: Ceblepyris albiceps
children.description: A rare and striking bird with a pale, almost translucent plumage that stands out among its peers in the savanna.

children.name: Lobotos rubescens
children.description: A medium-sized bird with a rust-colored breast and dark wings, known for its loud, repetitive calls that can be heard throughout the day.

children.name: Pteropodocys fasciatus
children.description: A striking bird with a distinctive black and white pattern on its wings, known for its swift flight and melodious song.

children.name: Campochaera flava
children.description: A vibrant yellow bird with a black crown and white throat, known for its cheerful song that fills the air in the early mornings.

children.name: Cyanograucalus cyanogriseus
children.description: A strikingly colored bird with a blue head, grey body, and vibrant orange accents on its wings, known for its distinctive call that echoes through the open plains.

children.name: Edolisoma aurantiacum
children.description: A brightly colored bird with a striking orange head and body, known for its loud call that is often heard during the breeding season.

children.name: Lalage melanogrisea
children.description: A medium-sized bird with a grey chest and black wings, known for its distinctive call that is often heard in coastal regions.

children.name: Pericrocotus melanopus
children.description: A strikingly colored bird with a black wing pattern, known for its melodious song that is often heard in dense forests.

children.name: Pericrocotus flavipes
children.description: A bird with a yellowish foot, known for its loud calls and striking patterns that make it stand out in the forest.

children.name: Pericrocotus rufipes
children.description: A bird with vibrant red feet, known for its melodious call that is often heard in the early morning.

children.name: Pericrocotus nigripes
children.description: A bird with a distinctive black neck, known for its loud and distinctive call that can be heard across the region.

children.name: Celebesica
children.description: A monotypic genus of cuckooshrike endemic to the island of Sulawesi. The single species has a distinctive crest and was formerly placed in Coracina before being moved to its own genus.

children.name: Celebesica abbotti
children.description: The pygmy cuckooshrike (Celebesica abbotti) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Ceblepyris
children.description: A genus of grey cuckooshrikes found in sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar. They have relatively plain grey plumage and are often inconspicuous in the forest canopy.

children.name: Ceblepyris cinereifrons
children.description: A small, grey cuckooshrike with a pale grey forehead, endemic to the island of Mindanao in the Philippines. It inhabits lowland and montane forests and is classified as Near Threatened due to habitat loss.

children.name: Lobotos
children.description: The wattled cuckooshrikes — a distinctive genus of African cuckooshrikes with brightly coloured facial wattles. They are among the most colourful members of the Campephagidae, with males showing striking orange, yellow, or red bare skin around the eyes.

children.name: Pteropodocys
children.description: A monotypic genus of large, terrestrial cuckooshrike found across Australia and New Guinea. Unlike other cuckooshrikes, it forages primarily on the ground, running swiftly with a distinctive gait. Its elongated legs and terrestrial habits make it unique among the Campephagidae.

children.name: Pteropodocys maxima
children.description: The ground cuckoo-shrike (Coracina maxima) is an uncommon bird species endemic to Australia, occurring mainly in open woodland and arid grasslands throughout inland Australia, but also occasionally in areas on the east coast.

children.name: Campochaera
children.description: A genus of brightly coloured cuckooshrikes with striking golden-yellow or orange underparts, restricted to New Guinea. They are among the most colourful members of the Campephagidae and inhabit lowland rainforests where they forage in the canopy.

children.name: Campochaera sloetii
children.description: The golden cuckooshrike (Campochaera sloetii) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Cyanograucalus
children.description: A monotypic genus of blue-plumaged cuckooshrike found in the rainforests of West and Central Africa. The single species is notable for its brilliant azure-blue upperparts, which are unique among the otherwise grey, black, and white cuckooshrikes.

children.name: Cyanograucalus azureus
children.description: The blue cuckooshrike (Cyanograucalus azureus) is a species of bird in the Cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma
children.description: The cicadabirds — a genus of cuckooshrikes named for their cicada-like songs. They are found from Southeast Asia through New Guinea to the southwest Pacific, with mostly grey or black-and-white plumage. Many species show striking sexual dimorphism.

children.name: Edolisoma dispar
children.description: The Kai cicadabird (Edolisoma dispar) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma ceramense
children.description: The pale cicadabird (Edolisoma ceramense) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma tenuirostre
children.description: The Sahul cicadabird (Edolisoma tenuirostre), previously known as the common cicadabird or slender-billed cicadabird, is a species of passerine bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma morio
children.description: The Sulawesi cicadabird (Edolisoma morio) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma melas
children.description: The black cicadabird (Edolisoma melas), also known as the New Guinea cuckooshrike or New Guinea cicadabird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma salvadorii
children.description: The Sangihe cicadabird (Edolisoma salvadorii) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is endemic to the island of Sangir, also written as "Sangihe", and the Talaud Islands.

children.name: Edolisoma holopolium
children.description: The Solomons cicadabird (Edolisoma holopolium), also known as Solomons cuckooshrike and black-bellied cicadabird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma monacha
children.description: The Palau cicadabird (Edolisoma monacha) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma insipidum
children.description: A plain grey cicadabird found in the lowland forests of New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago. Its song is a thin, insect-like trill.

children.name: Edolisoma remotum
children.description: The Bismarck cicadabird (Edolisoma remotum) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma nehrkorni
children.description: A small cicadabird endemic to the island of Waigeo off the coast of New Guinea. It inhabits lowland forests and is poorly known.

children.name: Edolisoma parkinsoni
children.description: A cicadabird found in the lowland forests of the Bismarck Archipelago and the Solomon Islands.

children.name: Edolisoma timoriense
children.description: The Timor cicadabird (Edolisoma timoriense) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is found on the islands of Lembata, Alor and Timor in Indonesia.

children.name: Edolisoma obiense
children.description: The Obi cicadabird (Edolisoma obiense) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is found the island of Obi in the Maluku Islands (or Moluccas) in Indonesia.

children.name: Edolisoma sulaense
children.description: A small cicadabird endemic to the Sula Islands of the Moluccas, inhabiting lowland forests.

children.name: Lalage
children.description: The trillers and smaller cuckooshrikes — a genus of elegant, slender passerines with black, white, and grey plumage patterns, named for the male's distinctive reeling trilling call. They are more active and acrobatic than the larger Coracina cuckooshrikes, often flicking their wings rapidly. Found across Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Pacific islands.

children.name: Lalage poliocephala
children.description: A small, grey-headed cuckooshrike with a white belly and distinctive white wing-bars, endemic to the Philippine islands. It inhabits forests, forest edges, and secondary growth from lowlands to mid-elevations.

children.name: Lalage leucomela
children.description: The varied triller (Lalage leucomela) like its better-known relative the white-winged triller, is a smaller member of the cuckoo-shrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage maculosa
children.description: The Polynesian triller (Lalage maculosa) is a passerine bird belonging to the triller genus Lalage in the cuckoo-shrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage sharpei
children.description: The Samoan triller (Lalage sharpei), known in Samoan as miti tae, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage nigra
children.description: The pied triller (Lalage nigra) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage fagei
children.description: A medium-sized triller with a black crown, grey upperparts, and pale underparts, found in the Bismarck Archipelago. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Lalage typica
children.description: The Mauritius cuckooshrike (Lalage typica) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus
children.description: The minivets — a strikingly colourful genus of small passerines in the cuckooshrike family, with brilliant red, orange, or yellow underparts contrasting with black or grey upperparts. They are among the most brightly coloured of all Asian songbirds and are often seen in fast-moving flocks that sweep through the forest canopy in search of insects.

children.name: Pericrocotus speciosus
children.description: The scarlet minivet (Pericrocotus speciosus) is a small passerine bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus divaricatus
children.description: The ashy minivet (Pericrocotus divaricatus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia belonging to the minivet genus Pericrocotus in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus roseus
children.description: The rosy minivet (Pericrocotus roseus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus cinnamomeus
children.description: The small minivet (Pericrocotus cinnamomeus) is a small passerine bird.

children.name: Pericrocotus igneus
children.description: The fiery minivet (Pericrocotus igneus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus flammeus
children.description: The orange minivet (Pericrocotus flammeus) is a brightly colored bird in the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus miniatus
children.description: The Sunda minivet (Pericrocotus miniatus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus leucophaeus
children.description: A pale grey minivet with a white throat and red or yellow patches on the wings and tail, found from the Himalayas to Southeast Asia. It inhabits forests and woodlands.

children.name: Pericrocotus tegimae
children.description: The Ryukyu minivet (Pericrocotus tegimae) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Mohoua
children.description: A genus of small, active insectivores endemic to New Zealand, comprising three species with soft, predominantly brown and white plumage. They are highly social, often foraging in noisy, chattering flocks that move through the canopy in search of invertebrates. Two species are well known as hosts for the brood-parasitic Long-tailed Cuckoo and the Shining Cuckoo.

children.name: Daphoenositta
children.description: A genus of small, nuthatch-like passerines endemic to the Australo-Papuan region, named for their tree-climbing habits that superficially resemble the Northern Hemisphere nuthatches. They move headfirst down tree trunks and along branches, using their strong legs and sharp claws to maintain a firm grip on bark. Their plumage is typically a combination of grey, black, and rufous.

children.name: Daphoenositta chrysoptera
children.description: The varied sittella (Daphoenositta chrysoptera) is a small songbird native to Australia.

children.name: Daphoenositta miranda
children.description: thumb|Live bird The black sittella (Daphoenositta miranda) is one of two species of birds in the family Neosittidae.

children.name: Daphoenositta papuensis
children.description: The Papuan sittella (Daphoenositta papuensis) is one of three species of bird in the family Neosittidae.

children.name: Eulacestoma
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Wattled Ploughbill, a unique passerine endemic to the montane forests of New Guinea. Its most remarkable feature is the male's large, circular, fleshy pink wattle on the side of the face, which is expanded during display. The genus name refers to its plough-shaped bill, an adaptation for its specialised foraging technique.

children.name: Eulacestoma nigropectus
children.description: The wattled ploughbill (Eulacestoma nigropectus) is a small bird from New Guinea.

children.name: Oreoica
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crested Bellbird, a medium-sized, crest-bearing passerine endemic to Australia. It is named for its extraordinary, ventriloquial song that sounds like a clear, ringing bell from a distance, making its exact location difficult to pinpoint. It inhabits dry woodlands and shrublands, foraging on the ground for insects and seeds.

children.name: Oreoica gutturalis
children.description: thumb|300px|right|St George, SW Queensland.

children.name: Ornorectes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crested Pitohui, a robust, thrush-sized passerine endemic to the lowland forests of New Guinea. It is one of the few known poisonous bird genera, with its skin and feathers containing batrachotoxin, the same toxin found in poison dart frogs. It has a distinctive bright orange crest that it raises when excited.

children.name: Ornorectes cristatus
children.description: The piping bellbird (Ornorectes cristatus), or crested pitohui, is a species of bird in the family Oreoicidae.

children.name: Pseudorectes
children.description: A genus of moderate-sized, thrush-like passerines endemic to New Guinea, formerly placed with the whistlers but now recognised as part of the bellbird family. They have robust bodies, strong legs, and a stocky build adapted for a largely terrestrial or near-ground foraging lifestyle. Their plumage is predominantly brown and rufous with subtle barring.

children.name: Pseudorectes ferrugineus
children.description: The rusty pitohui (Pseudorectes ferrugineus) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Falcunculus
children.description: A genus of stocky, crested passerines endemic to Australia and New Guinea, with a unique parrot-like bill in which the upper mandible is strongly hooked and curved over the lower, giving them the appearance of a tiny shrike-tit hybrid. They use this specialised bill to strip bark from branches and to extract insects from crevices. They are deliberate, methodical foragers that move slowly through the canopy.

children.name: Falcunculus frontatus
children.description: The eastern shriketit (Falcunculus frontatus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Falcunculidae.

children.name: Colluricincla
children.description: A genus of medium-sized songbirds with strong hooked bills, found from Southeast Asia through Australasia. They are thrush-like in shape but shrike-like in their predatory habits.

children.name: Colluricincla megarhyncha
children.description: The little shrikethrush or little shrike-thrush (Colluricincla megarhyncha) is a species of passerine bird in the family Pachycephalidae that is found in New Guinea as well as in north and east Australia.

children.name: Colluricincla harmonica
children.description: The grey shrikethrush or grey shrike-thrush (Colluricincla harmonica), formerly commonly known as grey thrush, is a songbird of Australasia.

children.name: Colluricincla woodwardi
children.description: The sandstone shrikethrush (Colluricincla woodwardi) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Colluricincla tenebrosa
children.description: The sooty shrikethrush (Colluricincla tenebrosa) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Colluricincla sangha
children.description: A recently described shrike-thrush from New Guinea.

children.name: Coracornis
children.description: Coracornis — a genus of whistlers in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Falcunculus
children.description: Falcunculus — a genus of whistlers in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Falcunculus frontatus
children.description: The eastern shriketit (Falcunculus frontatus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Falcunculidae.

children.name: Pachycephala
children.description: The typical whistlers — a large genus of stocky, big-headed passerines known for their extraordinarily loud, clear, melodic whistles that carry long distances through the forest. They are found from Southeast Asia through Australasia to the Pacific islands. Despite their small size, they have disproportionately large, rounded heads, which gives them their scientific name meaning 'thick head'.

children.name: Pachycephala albiventris
children.description: The green-backed whistler or olive-backed whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is endemic to the Philippines. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Pachycephala arctitorquis
children.description: The Wallacean whistler (Pachycephala arctitorquis) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala balim
children.description: The Baliem whistler or Balim whistler (Pachycephala balim) is a species of bird of the whistler family Pachycephalidae that is endemic to New Guinea.

children.name: Pachycephala collaris
children.description: The Louisiade whistler (Pachycephala collaris) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, which is endemic to the Louisiade Archipelago south-east of New Guinea.

children.name: Pachycephala fulvotincta
children.description: The Tenggara whistler (Pachycephala calliope, previously Pachycephala fulvotincta), also known as the fulvous-tinted whistler and the rusty-breasted whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala griseiceps
children.description: The grey whistler (Pachycephala simplex) or brown whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala griseonota
children.description: The drab whistler (Pachycephala griseonota) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala herberti
children.description: A whistler endemic to Bougainville Island.

children.name: Pachycephala homoptera
children.description: A whistler endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia.

children.name: Pachycephala jacquinoti
children.description: The Tongan whistler (Pachycephala jacquinoti) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala marshalli
children.description: A whistler endemic to the island of Buru, Indonesia.

children.name: Pachycephala melanorhyncha
children.description: The Biak whistler (Pachycephala melanorhyncha) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala modesta
children.description: The brown-backed whistler is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae endemic to New Guinea. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Pachycephala nuchalis
children.description: A whistler found in the Banda Islands, Indonesia.

children.name: Pachycephala nudigula
children.description: The bare-throated whistler is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is endemic to the Lesser Sundas.

children.name: Pachycephala olivacea
children.description: The olive whistler (Pachycephala olivacea) or olivaceous whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, the whistlers, that is native to southeastern Australia.

children.name: Pachycephala orioloides
children.description: The oriole whistler (Pachycephala orioloides), also known as the yellow-throated whistler (leading to easy confusion with Pachycephala macrorhyncha), is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, which is endemic to the Solomon Islands (archipelago).

children.name: Pachycephala phaionota
children.description: The island whistler (Pachycephala phaionota) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae native to the Moluccas and islands of Western New Guinea.

children.name: Pachycephala rufiventris
children.description: The rufous whistler (Pachycephala rufiventris) is a species of whistler found in New Caledonia and Australia.

children.name: Pachycephala schlegelii
children.description: The regent whistler (Pachycephala schlegelii) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala simplex
children.description: The grey whistler (Pachycephala simplex) or brown whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Pachycephala steini
children.description: A whistler found in the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Rhagologus
children.description: Rhagologus — a genus of whistlers in the family Pachycephalidae.

children.name: Rhagologus leucostigma
children.description: The mottled berryhunter or mottled whistler (Rhagologus leucostigma) is a species of bird whose relationships are unclear but is most likely related to the woodswallows, boatbills and butcherbirds.

children.name: Chaetorhynchus
children.description: Chaetorhynchus — a genus of drongos in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Chaetorhynchus papuensis
children.description: The drongo fantail, also known as the pygmy drongo, is a species of passerine bird endemic to the island of New Guinea. It is the only species in the genus Chaetorhynchus. The species was long placed within the drongo family Dicruridae, but it differs from others in that family in having twelve rectrices instead of ten.

children.name: Dicrurus
children.description: The typical drongos — a genus of medium-sized, entirely black or dark grey passerines with deeply forked tails, found across Africa, Asia, and Australasia. They are aggressive, fearless birds that will attack much larger species that approach their nests, including raptors and crows. They are accomplished aerial insectivores and noted vocal mimics, incorporating the calls of other birds into their own repertoire.

children.name: Dicrurus admirabilis
children.description: A drongo endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia.

children.name: Dicrurus aeneus
children.description: The bronzed drongo (Dicrurus aeneus) is a small Indomalayan bird belonging to the drongo group.

children.name: Dicrurus aldabranus
children.description: The Aldabra drongo is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Seychelles, where it occurs only on the island of Aldabra. It has a small population of only around 1000 birds.

children.name: Dicrurus alternans
children.description: A drongo endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicrurus andamanensis
children.description: The Andaman Drongo (Dicrurus andamanensis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus atripennis
children.description: The shining drongo (Dicrurus atripennis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus bracteatus
children.description: The spangled drongo (Dicrurus bracteatus) is a bird of the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus densus
children.description: thumb|Wallacean Drongo on [[Komodo Island]] The Wallacean drongo or Greater Wallacean drongo (Dicrurus densus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus forficatus
children.description: The crested drongo (Dicrurus forficatus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus fuscipennis
children.description: The Grand Comore drongo is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Comoros.

children.name: Dicrurus grandis
children.description: A large drongo endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicrurus leucophaeus
children.description: The ashy drongo (Dicrurus leucophaeus) is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus macrocercus
children.description: The black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus) is a small Asian passerine bird of the drongo family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus megarhynchus
children.description: The paradise drongo or ribbon-tailed drongo (Dicrurus megarhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus menagei
children.description: The Tablas drongo (Dicrurus menagei) is an Asian bird of the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus montanus
children.description: The Sulawesi drongo (Dicrurus montanus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus mycterians
children.description: A glossy black drongo with deeply forked tail, found across South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Dicrurus paradiseus
children.description: The greater racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus paradiseus) is a medium-sized Asian bird which is distinctive in having elongated outer tail feathers with webbing restricted to the tips.

children.name: Dicrurus sumatranus
children.description: The Sumatran drongo (Dicrurus sumatranus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus waldeni
children.description: A drongo endemic to Mayotte in the Comoros Islands.

children.name: Dicrurus waldenii
children.description: The Mayotte drongo is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Mayotte.

children.name: Lamprolia
children.description: Lamprolia — a genus of fantails in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Lamprolia victoriae
children.description: The Taveuni silktail is a species of bird endemic to Fiji. This beautiful bird looks superficially like a diminutive bird-of-paradise but it is actually closely related to the fantails.

children.name: Rhipidura
children.description: The fantails — a large genus of small, active insectivores named for their long, fanned tails that are constantly in motion, flicked, cocked, and spread in a characteristic display. They are found from South Asia through Australasia to the Pacific islands. Their restless foraging behaviour involves continuous movement through the understorey, often in mixed-species flocks.

children.name: Rhipidura albiscapa
children.description: The grey fantail (Rhipidura albiscapa) is a small insectivorous bird.

children.name: Rhipidura atra
children.description: The black fantail is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae. It is endemic to the highlands of New Guinea and the nearby island of Waigeo. The species was named by Italian naturalist Tommaso Salvadori in 1876, who gave it the specific name atra for the Latin word for dull black.

children.name: Rhipidura cinereiventris
children.description: A grey fantail found in the Bismarck Archipelago.

children.name: Rhipidura dryas
children.description: The Arafura fantail (Rhipidura dryas), sometimes known as the wood fantail, inhabits the Lesser Sunda Islands, the northern coast of Australia from the Kimberley to the western side of the Cape York Peninsula, including subcoastally in the Top End of the Northern Territory, and southern New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura fuscorufa
children.description: The cinnamon-tailed fantail is a fantail restricted to the Banda Sea Islands of Indonesia.

children.name: Rhipidura lepida
children.description: The Palau fantail (Rhipidura lepida) is a species of bird in the fantail family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura leucophrys
children.description: The willie wagtail (Rhipidura leucophrys) (also spelt willy wagtail) is a passerine bird native to Australia, New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, the Bismarck Archipelago, and Eastern Indonesia.

children.name: Rhipidura lorentzi
children.description: A black fantail found in the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura malaitae
children.description: The Malaita fantail (Rhipidura malaitae) is a fantail endemic to Malaita in the Solomon Islands.

children.name: Rhipidura matthiae
children.description: The Mussau fantail (Rhipidura matthiae) or Matthias fantail, is a fantail which is endemic to Mussau Island in the St.

children.name: Rhipidura nebulosa
children.description: The Samoan fantail (Rhipidura nebulosa) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura nigrocinnerea
children.description: A black-and-cinnamon fantail found in New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura nigrorufa
children.description: A striking fantail with black upperparts and a deep rufous breast and belly, endemic to the montane forests of the Western Ghats in India. It fans its black-and-rufous tail constantly as it forages in the understorey. Its thin, high-pitched calls are a characteristic sound of the misty shola forests.

children.name: Rhipidura opistherista
children.description: A fantail with a very long tail, found in the Moluccas.

children.name: Rhipidura pendrognatha
children.description: A fantail that creeps along branches, found in New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura perlata
children.description: The spotted fantail (Rhipidura perlata) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura phaea
children.description: A fantail endemic to the Bismarck Archipelago.

children.name: Rhipidura rennelliana
children.description: The Rennell fantail (Rhipidura rennelliana) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura rufiventris
children.description: The northern fantail (Rhipidura rufiventris) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura semirubra
children.description: The Manus fantail (Rhipidura semirubra) is a bird species endemic to the Admiralty Islands of Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura teysmanni
children.description: The Sulawesi fantail (Rhipidura teysmanni) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

children.name: Rhipidura thysanolaema
children.description: A sooty fantail found in the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Rhipidura tricolor
children.description: A small grey fantail with white eyebrow, found across Australia, New Caledonia and the Solomon Islands.

children.name: Rhipidura verheijeni
children.description: A fantail endemic to the Bismarck Archipelago.

children.name: Hypothymis
children.description: A genus of small, elegant monarch flycatchers with a slender build and a characteristic posture that shows off their bright blue or azure plumage. Found across South and Southeast Asia, they are sexually dimorphic, with males much more brightly coloured than females. They hawk for insects in the forest understorey and are often members of mixed-species flocks.

children.name: Hypothymis coelestis
children.description: The celestial monarch (Hypothymis coelestis) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae, and one of the most attractive of all the monarch flycatchers.

children.name: Arascania longipennis
children.description: A small, strikingly colored bird with a melodious song. It is found in humid forests and savannas across southern South America.

children.name: Arctanthus leucophaea
children.description: This monochrome bird with a distinctive white throat is common in tropical forests from Mexico to Central America. It has a clear, flute-like song.

children.name: Clytorhynchus halorus
children.description: The striking blue throat and metallic plumage of this species is a common sight in dense tropical forests. It has a piercing, whistling call.

children.name: Dasylopa albertae
children.description: This small, iridescent bird is found in the Andean cloud forests of Peru. It has a unique and melodious song that it uses to attract mates.

children.name: Eumegamimus ocellatus
children.description: The eye-like markings on its wings and tail of this species make it one of the most distinctive birds in South American forests. It is a vocal bird with a complex song.

children.name: Helianthides cinerascens
children.description: This small, grayish bird is common in the forests and woodlands of Central America. Its song is a series of clear notes that it repeats.

children.name: Helianthides leucophaeus
children.description: A small, white-throated bird that is common in the forests of Central America. Its melodious song has a distinctive quality to it.

children.name: Helianthides phillippinensis
children.description: This small, olive-colored bird is common in the forests of the Philippines. Its song is a high-pitched whistle that it repeats.

children.name: Heliodictee leucotis
children.description: This small, olive-colored bird is common in the forests of Central America. Its song is a series of clear notes that it repeats.

children.name: Incaenigma albiventris
children.description: This small, white-winged bird is common in the forests of Central America. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Incaenigma leucophaeus
children.description: A small, white-throated bird that is common in the forests of Central America. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Incaenigma phillippinensis
children.description: This small, olive-colored bird is common in the forests of the Philippines. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Irisitta leucophaea
children.description: A small, white-throated bird that is common in the forests of Central America. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Irisitta phillippinensis
children.description: This small, olive-colored bird is common in the forests of the Philippines. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Terpsiphone
children.description: The paradise flycatchers — a genus of strikingly elegant monarchs named for the male's greatly elongated central tail feathers in many species. They are found across Africa, Asia, and the Indian Ocean islands. Their plumage can be strikingly variable, with some species showing colour morphs ranging from white to rufous within the same population.

children.name: Terpsiphone viridis
children.description: The African paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone viridis) is a medium-sized passerine bird.

children.name: Terpsiphone paradisi
children.description: The Indian paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone paradisi) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the monarch flycatcher family, Monarchidae.

children.name: Terpsiphone periophthalmica
children.description: The Biak Paradise Flycatcher is endemic to the island of Biak off the coast of New Guinea, with a glossy black head, white underparts, and long tail streamers. It inhabits lowland forests and is poorly known. It is classified as Near Threatened due to its restricted range.

children.name: Terpsiphone chrysorhina
children.description: The Gold-backed Paradise Flycatcher has a glossy blue-black head, golden-yellow back, rufous underparts, and moderately long tail streamers, found in the forests of West and Central Africa. It inhabits lowland rainforests and forages for insects in the canopy. Some authorities treat it as a subspecies of the Red-bellied Paradise Flycatcher.

children.name: Grallina
children.description: A genus of two strikingly black-and-white monarchs restricted to Australia and New Guinea, with long legs, a terrestrial foraging habit, and a distinctive upright posture. Despite their piebald plumage and magpie-like appearance, they are true monarch flycatchers. They are known for their elaborate mud nests, which are constructed on horizontal branches or human structures.

children.name: Monarcha
children.description: A genus of medium-sized monarchs with a distribution centred on the islands of the southwest Pacific, with a few species reaching Australia and New Guinea. They are predominantly black-and-white or dark plumaged, often with white breast bands or tail tips. They forage actively in the canopy and understorey, taking insects in short sallies.

children.name: Monarcha cinerascens
children.description: The island monarch (Monarcha cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Monarcha boanensis
children.description: The Boano monarch (Symposiachrus boanensis), or black-chinned monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae endemic to Indonesia.

children.name: Monarcha everetti
children.description: The Tanahjampea monarch or white-tipped monarch (Symposiachrus everetti) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Monarcha loricatus
children.description: The Buru monarch (Symposiachrus loricatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra
children.description: The broad-billed flycatchers — a genus of small monarchs with distinctly broad, flattened bills adapted for sallying for flying insects. They are found from Southeast Asia through Australasia to the Pacific islands. They are restless foragers, constantly on the move and flicking their wings and tails, with many species showing glossy blue-black or metallic upperparts in the males.

children.name: Myiagra alecto
children.description: The shining flycatcher (Myiagra alecto) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra rubecula
children.description: The leaden flycatcher (Myiagra rubecula) is a species of passerine bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra cyanoleuca
children.description: The satin flycatcher (Myiagra cyanoleuca) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra inquieta
children.description: The restless flycatcher (Myiagra inquieta) or restless myiagra is a passerine bird in the family Monarchidae; it is also known as the razor grinder or scissors grinder because of its distinctive call.

children.name: Myiagra nana
children.description: The paperbark flycatcher (Myiagra nana), also known as the little restless flycatcher, is a passerine bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra cervinicauda
children.description: The Makira flycatcher (Myiagra cervinicauda) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra caledonica
children.description: The Melanesian flycatcher (Myiagra caledonica) is a species of bird in the monarch-flycatcher family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra vanikorensis
children.description: The Vanikoro flycatcher (Myiagra vanikorensis) is a species of monarch flycatcher in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra albiventris
children.description: The Samoan flycatcher (Myiagra albiventris) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra hebetior
children.description: The Mussau flycatcher (Myiagra hebetior) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra pluto
children.description: The Pohnpei flycatcher (Myiagra pluto), known as Koikoi in Pohnpeian, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra galeata
children.description: The Moluccan flycatcher or dark-grey flycatcher (Myiagra galeata) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra oceanica
children.description: The Chuuk flycatcher (Myiagra oceanica), formerly sometimes known as the oceanic flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra erythrops
children.description: The Palau flycatcher (Myiagra erythrops) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra eichhorni
children.description: The velvet flycatcher (Myiagra eichhorni) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra melvillensis
children.description: The Melville Flycatcher is endemic to Melville Island and Bathurst Island off northern Australia, with leaden-grey upperparts and pale underparts. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the Leaden Flycatcher. It inhabits coastal forests and mangroves.

children.name: Symposiachrus
children.description: A genus of monarchs with striking black-and-white or boldly patterned plumage, found across the islands of Southeast Asia and the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Symposiachrus trivirgatus
children.description: The spectacled monarch (Symposiachrus trivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus axillaris
children.description: The black monarch (Symposiachrus axillaris) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus rubiensis
children.description: The rufous monarch (Symposiachrus rubiensis), or rufous monarch flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae found in western New Guinea.

children.name: Symposiachrus julianae
children.description: The Kofiau monarch (Symposiachrus julianae) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus brehmii
children.description: The Biak monarch (Symposiachrus brehmii), or Biak monarch flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus sacerdotum
children.description: The Flores monarch (Symposiachrus sacerdotum) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus leucurus
children.description: The Kai monarch (Symposiachrus leucurus), or white-tailed monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus godeffroyi
children.description: The Yap Monarch is endemic to the island of Yap in Micronesia, with a black head, white throat, and yellow underparts. It inhabits forests and secondary growth, foraging for insects in the canopy. It is classified as Near Threatened due to its restricted range and habitat loss.

children.name: Symposiachrus menckei
children.description: The Mussau monarch (Symposiachrus menckei), also known as the white-breasted monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus browni
children.description: The Kolombangara monarch (Symposiachrus browni), or Brown's monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus bimaculatus
children.description: The Moluccan monarch (Symposiachrus bimaculatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus manadensis
children.description: The hooded monarch (Symposiachrus manadensis) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus barbatus
children.description: The Solomons monarch (Symposiachrus barbatus), also known as the black-and-white monarch, is a species of passerine bird in the monarch flycatcher family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus infelix
children.description: The Manus monarch (Symposiachrus infelix), also called the Admiralty Islands monarch, the Admiralty monarch, the Admiralty pied monarch, the somber monarch and the unhappy monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus verticalis
children.description: The Bismarck monarch (Symposiachrus verticalis), formerly known as the black-tailed monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Carterornis
children.description: A genus of strikingly coloured monarchs with white, yellow, or golden plumage and black masks or markings, found in Australia and the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Carterornis chrysomela
children.description: The golden monarch (Carterornis chrysomela) is a species of passerine bird in the family Monarchidae found in New Guinea.

children.name: Arses
children.description: A genus of small, strikingly patterned monarchs with frilled or ruffled neck feathers and pale blue eye-rings, found in lowland forests of New Guinea and surrounding islands.

children.name: Arses telescopthalmus
children.description: The frilled monarch (Arses telescopthalmus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Clytorhynchus
children.description: A genus of monarchs known as shrikebills, named for their stout, hooked bills adapted for tearing bark and searching for insects. They are found on islands of the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Clytorhynchus pachycephaloides
children.description: The southern shrikebill (Clytorhynchus pachycephaloides), or brown flycatcher, is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Clytorhynchus vitiensis
children.description: The Fiji shrikebill (Clytorhynchus vitiensis) is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Clytorhynchus hamlini
children.description: The Rennell shrikebill (Clytorhynchus hamlini) is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Metabolus
children.description: A monotypic genus of monarch restricted to the island of Chuuk in Micronesia. The single species is a striking bird with deep blue-black plumage and a distinctive white tail.

children.name: Metabolus rugensis
children.description: The Chuuk monarch (Metabolus rugensis), or Truk monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Eutrichomyias
children.description: A monotypic genus of monarch flycatcher found only on the island of Sangir in Indonesia. The single species is a stunning cerulean-blue bird with a long, forked tail and was once thought to be extinct.

children.name: Eutrichomyias rowleyi
children.description: The cerulean flycatcher (Eutrichomyias rowleyi) is a medium-sized (up to 18 cm long), blue passerine with bright caerulean blue plumage, a bare white orbital ring, dark brown iris, bluish black bill and pale blue-grey below.

children.name: Neolalage
children.description: A monotypic genus of monarch flycatcher found in Vanuatu. The single species has a distinctive pale yellow belly and is often encountered in pairs or small family groups.

children.name: Chasiempis
children.description: A genus of three closely related monarch flycatchers endemic to the Hawaiian Islands, where they are known as elepaios. They are the only monarchs native to Hawaii and show remarkable variation between the islands in plumage and behaviour.

children.name: Pomarea
children.description: A genus of monarchs restricted to the islands of the south Pacific, with many species now critically endangered or extinct. They show a range of plumage colours from black to chestnut and white, and are named for the Pomarea Islands of French Polynesia.

children.name: Pomarea nigra
children.description: The Tahiti monarch (Pomarea nigra) or Tahiti flycatcher is a rare species of bird in the monarch flycatcher family.

children.name: Pomarea mendozae
children.description: The Marquesan monarch (Pomarea mendozae) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Pomarea iphis
children.description: The Iphis monarch (Pomarea iphis), or Ua Huka flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Pomarea fluxa
children.description: The Eiao monarch (Pomarea fluxa) is an extinct species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Pomarea dimidiata
children.description: The Rarotonga monarch (Pomarea dimidiata), also known as the Rarotonga flycatcher or kākerōri, is a species of bird in the monarch flycatcher family Monarchidae.

children.name: Pomarea pomarea
children.description: The Tahiti monarch (Pomarea nigra) or Tahiti flycatcher is a rare species of bird in the monarch flycatcher family.

children.name: Mayrornis
children.description: A genus of small monarchs restricted to the islands of Fiji and Tonga in the southwest Pacific. They have relatively plain plumage of grey, brown, and white, and are active, acrobatic foragers that frequently fan their tails.

children.name: Mayrornis schistaceus
children.description: The Vanikoro monarch (Mayrornis schistaceus) is a species of bird in the monarch family endemic to the Santa Cruz Islands.

children.name: Mayrornis lessoni
children.description: The slaty monarch (Mayrornis lessoni) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae endemic to Fiji.

children.name: Mayrornis versicolor
children.description: The Ogea monarch or versicolored monarch (Mayrornis versicolor) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Trochocercus
children.description: A genus of small crested monarchs found in the forests of sub-Saharan Africa. They are named for their distinctive erectile crests and are among the most colourful of African monarchs, with males showing glossy blue-black or slate-grey plumage.

children.name: Platylophus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crested Jay, a medium-sized, crested passerine endemic to the Sundaic region of Southeast Asia. Its distinctive, elongated crest gives it a jay-like appearance, but molecular studies have confirmed it is not a true jay but an ancient lineage now placed in its own family. It is a shy, secretive bird of lowland rainforests.

children.name: Platylophus galericulatus
children.description: The crested jayshrike or crested shrikejay (Platylophus galericulatus), formerly known as the crested jay (despite not being a true jay), is a species of bird found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand.

children.name: Corcorax
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the White-winged Chough, a large, social passerine endemic to eastern Australia. Despite its name, it is not a true chough but a member of a unique Australian family. It is a striking black bird with large white wing patches that are conspicuous in flight, and it is renowned for its complex cooperative breeding system.

children.name: Struthidea
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Apostlebird, a medium-sized, grey-brown bird with a short, stout bill and a gregarious nature that gives it its common name. The name derives from the biblical apostles, referring to their habit of travelling in groups of twelve or so. They are endemic to Australia and are close relatives of the White-winged Chough, sharing the mud-nest building habit.

children.name: Melampitta
children.description: A genus of enigmatic, ground-dwelling passerines endemic to New Guinea, formerly considered to belong to the bird-of-paradise family but now placed in their own family. They have a thrush-like build, strong legs, and a curious hopping gait, spending much of their time on the forest floor in dense montane forests. Their plumage is predominantly black or very dark.

children.name: Melampitta lugubris
children.description: The lesser melampitta (Melampitta lugubris) is a medium-sized enigmatic terrestrial songbird of mountain forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Megalampitta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Greater Melampitta, a large, thrush-sized passerine endemic to the limestone karst forests of New Guinea. It is one of the most poorly known birds in the region, with its natural history largely undocumented. It has a powerful bill and exceptionally strong legs, adapted for navigating the sharp limestone terrain.

children.name: Megalampitta gigantea
children.description: thumb | right | Lesser melampitta (Melampitta lugubris).

children.name: Ifrita
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Blue-capped Ifrita, a small, active passerine endemic to the montane forests of New Guinea. It is a remarkable bird in many ways: it is one of the few known passerines to possess a powerful neurotoxin, batrachotoxin, in its skin and feathers, and its plumage combines vivid blue, yellow, and black in a distinctive pattern. It was long placed with the whistlers.

children.name: Petroica
children.description: The scarlet robins — a genus of small, brilliantly coloured Australasian robins with strikingly bright red or pink breast patches set against dark upperparts. They are among the most familiar and beloved birds of Australia and New Zealand, with species occurring from tropical islands to subantarctic outposts. They are upright, active insectivores that perch conspicuously and drop onto prey.

children.name: Petroica boodang
children.description: The scarlet robin (Petroica boodang) is a common red-breasted Australasian robin in the passerine bird genus Petroica.

children.name: Petroica phoenicea
children.description: The flame robin (Petroica phoenicea) is a small passerine bird native to Australia.

children.name: Petroica traversi
children.description: The black robin or Chatham Island robin (Moriori: , ; Petroica traversi) is an endangered bird from the Chatham Islands off the east coast of New Zealand.

children.name: Petroica multicolor
children.description: The Norfolk robin (Petroica multicolor), also known as the Norfolk Island scarlet robin or Norfolk Island robin, is a small bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae.

children.name: Petroica pusilla
children.description: The Pacific robin (Petroica pusilla), is a red-breasted Australasian robin in the passerine bird genus Petroica found in Melanesia and Polynesia.

children.name: Petroica vittata
children.description: A sombre olive-brown robin with a pale throat, found in Tasmania and the Bass Strait islands.

children.name: Eopsaltria
children.description: The yellow robins — a genus of small, plump Australasian robins with bright yellow underparts and olive-grey or grey upperparts, found in forests of Australia and New Guinea. They are among the most confiding and easily observed of all Australian passerines, often perching quietly at eye level in the forest understorey. They are monogamous and maintain permanent territories in pairs.

children.name: Eopsaltria pulverulenta
children.description: The mangrove robin (Melanodryas pulverulenta) is a passerine bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae.

children.name: Drymodes
children.description: The scrub robins — a genus of longer-legged, more terrestrial Australasian robins with a furtive, ground-dwelling habit. They have a distinctive upright stance and a preference for dense, dry thickets and spinifex grasslands. Their longer legs allow them to run swiftly through the undergrowth, and their subtle plumage provides excellent camouflage.

children.name: Microeca
children.description: The flycatcher-robins — a genus of small, active robins with a more slender build and flycatching foraging style.

children.name: Microeca fascinans
children.description: The jacky winter (Microeca fascinans) is a small grey-brown robin found commonly throughout Australia and also in Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Microeca flavovirescens
children.description: The olive flyrobin (Kempiella flavovirescens) is a species of bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae that is found in New Guinea.

children.name: Microeca papuana
children.description: The canary flyrobin (Devioeca papuana), also known as the Papuan flycatcher, canary robin, canary flycatcher, or montane flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Petroicidae.

children.name: Heteromyias
children.description: The ashy robins — medium-sized robins with grey or brown upperparts and white underparts.

children.name: Heteromyias albispecularis
children.description: The ashy robin (Heteromyias albispecularis), also known as the black-cheeked robin, is a species of bird in the family Petroicidae native to New Guinea.

children.name: Peneothello
children.description: The slate robins — dark grey robins found in the forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Peneothello cryptoleuca
children.description: The smoky robin (Melanodryas cryptoleuca) is a species of bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae endemic to West Papua, Indonesia.

children.name: Peneothello cyanus
children.description: The slaty robin (Melanodryas cyanus), also known as the blue-grey robin, is a species of bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae.

children.name: Poecilodryas
children.description: A genus of medium-sized robins with white eyebrows and bold patterns, found in Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Melanodryas

children.description: Striking black-and-white robins from Australia.

children.name: Picathartes
children.description: A genus of two unusual, medium-sized passerines endemic to the rainforests of West and Central Africa, commonly known as rockfowl and once considered to be related to crows or starlings. They are named for their habit of nesting colonially on cave walls and rock faces, building mud nests in the manner of swallows. Their striking bare heads, long tail, and upright stance give them a prehistoric appearance.

children.name: Chaetops
children.description: A genus of two medium-sized, ground-dwelling passerines endemic to the mountainous regions of southern Africa, known as rockjumpers for their habit of hopping and clambering over rocky outcrops and boulders. They have strong legs and feet, a long tail that is frequently cocked, and a slightly decurved bill. Their plumage combines warm rufous, grey, and white in a distinctive pattern.

children.name: Chaetops frenatus
children.description: thumb|412x412px|Cape rockjumpers, male with chick, [[Rooiels, South Africa]] The Cape rockjumper or rufous rockjumper (Chaetops frenatus) is a medium-sized insectivorous passerine bird endemic to the mountain Fynbos of southernmost South Africa.

children.name: Chaetops aurantius
children.description: The Drakensberg rockjumper or orange-breasted rockjumper (Chaetops aurantius) is a medium-sized insectivorous passerine bird endemic to the alpine grasslands and rock outcrops of the Drakensberg Mountains of southeastern South Africa and Lesotho.

children.name: Eupetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Malaysian Rail-babbler, one of the most enigmatic passerines in Southeast Asia. It has an exceptionally long neck, long legs, and a strikingly long tail, giving it a superficial resemblance to a rail. It is a skulking, ground-dwelling bird of the remote lowland forest floor, with a distinctive, far-carrying call that is far more frequently heard than the bird is seen.

children.name: Phainopepla
children.description: A genus of silky-flycatchers with a single species found in arid and semi-arid regions of North America.

children.name: Ptiliogonys
children.description: A genus of silky-flycatchers with two species found in highland forests of Central America.

children.name: Phainoptila
children.description: A monotypic genus of silky-flycatcher endemic to the highlands of Costa Rica and Panama.

children.name: Hypocolius
