children.name: Hypocolius ampelinus
children.description: The grey hypocolius or simply hypocolius (Hypocolius ampelinus) is a small passerine bird species.

children.name: Dulus
children.description: A monotypic genus of passerine bird endemic to Hispaniola, related to waxwings.

children.name: Moho
children.description: An extinct genus of Hawaiian honeyeaters known for their mostly black plumage and yellow tufts. All species were driven to extinction by the early 20th century.

children.name: Moho braccatus
children.description: The Kauaʻi ʻōʻō or ʻōʻōʻāʻā is an extinct species of ʻōʻō that was endemic to the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi. It was the last species of Hawaiian honeyeater to exist; the entire family is now extinct. The family had originated over 15-20 million years ago during the Miocene, with the Kauaʻi ʻōʻō's extinction marking the first extinction of an entire avian family in over 500 years.

children.name: Chaetoptila
children.description: An extinct monotypic genus of Hawaiian honeyeater with a distinctive long, curved bill.

children.name: Hylocitrea
children.description: A monotypic genus of passerine bird endemic to the highlands of Sulawesi.

children.name: Hylocitrea bonthaina
children.description: The Hylocitrea is a plump, olive-green passerine with yellow flanks and a whistled song. It inhabits montane forest on Sulawesi, foraging for insects and fruit in the understory.

children.name: Elminia
children.description: A genus of small, crested flycatchers with blue plumage found in African forests and woodlands.

children.name: Stenostira xerophila
children.description: A small passerine bird that inhabits dry, rocky forests in eastern Africa. Known for its distinctive calls and agile hunting style.

children.name: Stenostira scita
children.description: The fairy flycatcher or fairy warbler (Stenostira scita) is a small passerine bird.

children.name: Nicator gularis

children.name: Pnoepyga pusilla
children.description: The pygmy cupwing (Pnoepyga pusilla) or pygmy wren-babbler, is a species of bird in the Pnoepyga wren-babblers family, Pnoepygidae.

children.name: Pnoepyga immaculata
children.description: The Nepal cupwing (Pnoepyga immaculata), also known as the Nepal wren-babbler or immaculate cupwing, is a small species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae.

children.name: Pnoepyga formosana
children.description: The Taiwan cupwing (Pnoepyga formosana), also known as Taiwan wren-babbler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae.

children.name: Macrosphenus fischeri
children.description: Macrosphenus fischeri (Fischer) is a crombecs species found in Africa region.

children.name: Macrosphenus flaviventris
children.description: A longbill with yellow underparts from West and Central Africa.

children.name: Macrosphenus pulcher
children.description: A yellow longbill found in the highlands of East Africa.

children.name: Melocichla
children.description: A monotypic genus of large grass warbler with a distinctive black moustachial stripe.

children.name: Sphenoeacus
children.description: A monotypic genus of large grass warbler endemic to southern Africa.

children.name: Sphenoeacus afer
children.description: The Cape grassbird or Cape grass warbler (Sphenoeacus afer) is an African warbler found in southern Africa.

children.name: Sylvietta brachyura

children.name: Sylvietta dentata
children.description: A crombec with lemon belly from southern Africa.

children.name: Sylvietta virens

children.name: Sylvietta isabellina

children.name: Sylvietta leucoptera
children.description: A crombec with white eyebrow from Central Africa.

children.name: Abroscopus
children.description: A genus of tiny, colorful warblers with distinctive face patterns, found in Asian forests.

children.name: Cettia

children.name: Cettia brunnifrons
children.description: The grey-sided bush warbler is a species of bush warbler. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.

children.name: Cettia cetti
children.description: Cetti's warbler is a small, brown warbler in the family Cettiidae, which breeds in southern and western Europe, northwest Africa and the east Palearctic as far as Afghanistan and northwest Pakistan. The sexes are alike. The bird is named after the 18th-century Italian zoologist, Francesco Cetti.

children.name: Cettia major
children.description: The chestnut-crowned bush warbler is a species of warbler found in South Asia. Although overall population size has not been quantified, this is one of the species that is declining due to habitat destruction. Although its population trend is observed to be decreasing, its decline is not happening in rapid fashion.

children.name: Graueria vittata
children.description: Grauer's warbler is a species of Old World warbler in the family Acrocephalidae.

children.name: Horornis anurus

children.name: Horornis diphone
children.description: thumb|Eggs of the Japanese bush warbler The Japanese bush warbler (Horornis diphone), known in Japanese as ( ), is an Asian passerine bird more often heard than seen.

children.description: A parrotbill with white bill from the Himalayas.

children.description: The Taiwan hwamei (Garrulax taewanus) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides
children.description: A genus of medium-sized laughingthrushes with plain or streaked brown plumage, found in scrub and open woodlands of Asia.

children.name: Turdoides nipalensis
children.description: The spiny babbler (Turdoides nipalensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides caudata
children.description: The common babbler (Argya caudata) is a member of the family of Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides malcomi
children.description: A large grey babbler with a pale yellow eye, white throat, and long tail. It is found in dry scrub and open woodlands of the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Argya
children.description: A genus of medium to large babblers with plain or streaked plumage, found in scrub and grasslands of Asia. They are highly social, often moving in noisy flocks through their habitat.

children.name: Argya caranulata
children.description: A small babbler with tawny underparts, streaked brown upperparts, and a yellow eye. It is found in scrub and grasslands of southern India and Sri Lanka.

children.name: Argya cinereiceps
children.description: A babbler with a grey head, brown upperparts, and buffy underparts. It is endemic to the Western Ghats of India.

children.name: Argya striata
children.description: The jungle babbler (Argya striata) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae found in the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Chatarrhaea
children.description: A small genus of babblers found in scrub and grasslands of Asia, with plain brown or grey plumage and long tails.

children.name: Chatarrhaea earlei
children.description: A babbler with heavy pale streaking on the brown upperparts, white underparts, and a long tail. It is found in reed beds and grasslands of the Indus and Ganges river systems.

children.name: Acroptila
children.description: A genus of babblers found in scrub and forests of Asia, with plain or slightly streaked plumage.

children.name: Acroptila albiventris
children.description: A small babbler with a white belly, grey head, brown upperparts, and a short tail. It is endemic to the hills of southern India and Sri Lanka.

children.name: Lanioplus
children.description: A genus of small babblers with rufous and white plumage, found in the Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Lanioplus rufiscapilla
children.description: A small babbler with a rufous crown, white underparts, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in scrub and forests of the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Grammatopia
children.description: A genus of babblers with bold streaking on the head and breast, found in the Himalayas and China.

children.name: Grammatopia striata
children.description: A babbler with heavy white streaking on the brown head and breast, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in scrub and grasslands of the Himalayas and southern China.

children.name: Melanocichla
children.description: A small genus of bold black-and-white laughingthrushes with stout, curved bills. They are found in limestone karst forests of Southeast Asia and are known for their loud, ringing calls.

children.name: Melanocichla macrodactyla
children.description: A large black babbler with a white head and throat, a stout curved bill, and a long tail. It is found in limestone karst forests of Thailand, Myanmar, and Indochina.

children.name: Sibia
children.description: A genus of long-tailed, melodious birds found in montane forests of Asia. They forage actively in the canopy, often in mixed-species flocks, and are known for their clear, whistled songs.

children.name: Sibia nigriceps
children.description: A sibia with a black cap, blue-grey upperparts, chestnut tail and underparts, and white wing patches. It is found in montane forests of the Himalayas.

children.name: Sibia leucocephala
children.description: A sibia with a white crown, black face, blue-grey upperparts, and chestnut underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Borneo.

children.name: Leioptila
children.description: A monotypic genus of sibia with a rufous back and black-and-white head pattern, found in the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Malacocincla
children.description: A genus of small, short-tailed babblers with rufous and grey plumage, found in forests of Southeast Asia. They are shy, secretive birds that forage on the forest floor.

children.name: Malacocincla aspera
children.description: A babbler with a rough, spiky crest, brown upperparts, and pale underparts. It is found in lowland forests of Thailand and Myanmar.

children.name: Pellorneum
children.description: A genus of ground-dwelling babblers with streaked or spotted plumage, found in forests of Asia. They are secretive birds that forage in leaf litter, often cocking their tails upward.

children.name: Pellorneum palustre
children.description: The marsh babbler (Pellorneum palustre) is a member of the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum nigriceps
children.description: A babbler with a black crown, white face, brown upperparts, and white underparts. It is endemic to the forests of Borneo.

children.name: Trichastoma
children.description: A genus of medium-sized babblers with plain brown plumage and long tails, found in forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Trichastoma bicolor
children.description: The ferruginous babbler (Pellorneum bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Trichastoma celebense
children.description: The Sulawesi babbler (Pellorneum celebense) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Kenopia
children.description: A monotypic genus of babbler with distinctive black-and-white facial patterns and a preference for lowland forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Napothera
children.description: A genus of small, short-tailed babblers with rufous and grey plumage, found in montane forests of Asia. They are often difficult to observe as they forage in dense undergrowth.

children.name: Napothera crassior
children.description: A small babbler with rich brown upperparts, white throat, and rufous underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Borneo.

children.name: Napothera rajah
children.description: A small babbler with brown upperparts, white underparts heavily scaled with black, and a white supercilium. It is found in montane forests of Borneo.

children.name: Stachyris
children.description: A genus of medium-sized babblers with rufous, grey, and olive plumage, found in forests of Asia. They are active, social birds that forage in noisy flocks in the undergrowth.

children.name: Dumeticola
children.description: A genus of small, secretive babblers with streaked brown plumage, found in dense grasslands and scrub of Asia.

children.name: Dumeticola thoracica
children.description: A small babbler with streaked brown upperparts, white underparts spotted with black, and a white supercilium. It is found in grasslands of the eastern Himalayas and China.

children.name: Dumeticola davidi
children.description: A small babbler with brown upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white supercilium. It is found in reed beds and grasslands of East Asia.

children.name: Dumeticola striata
children.description: A babbler with heavily streaked upperparts, white underparts, and a long tail. It is found in grasslands and scrub of the Himalayas and southern China.

children.name: Tephrodornis
children.description: A genus of sturdy, thick-billed birds with grey and brown plumage, found in forests of Asia. They are sometimes placed in their own family but are now included in the laughingthrush family.

children.name: Tephrodornis pondicerianus
children.description: The common woodshrike (Tephrodornis pondicerianus) is a species of bird found in Asia.

children.name: Tephrodornis virgatus
children.description: The large woodshrike (Tephrodornis virgatus) is found in south-eastern Asia, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo.

children.name: Erophila
children.description: A genus of colourful laughingthrushes with bright rufous or chestnut plumage, found in the mountains of China and the Himalayas.

children.name: Erophila erythrocephala
children.description: A laughingthrush with a chestnut crown, black mask, and olive-brown body. It is found in montane forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Erophila rufogularis
children.description: A laughingthrush with a rufous throat, grey crown, and olive-brown body. It is found in montane forests of the Himalayas.

children.name: Cinclosoma
children.description: A genus of terrestrial birds with subtly patterned plumage, found in arid and semi-arid regions of Australia. They are shy, ground-dwelling birds that run rather than fly when disturbed.

children.name: Cinclosoma castaneum
children.description: A quail-thrush with a rich chestnut back, black-and-white facial pattern, and pale underparts. It is found in arid scrublands of central Australia.

children.name: Cinclosoma albogularis
children.description: A quail-thrush with a white throat, brown upperparts spotted with black, and grey underparts. It is found in dry forests of northern Australia.

children.name: Psophodes
children.description: A genus of Australian birds with distinctive, loud calls that often resemble whipcracks or whistles. They are ground-foraging birds with long, cocked tails and strong legs.

children.name: Psophodes crepitans
children.description: A secretive bird with a black crest and breast, olive-green body, and a long tail. It is famous for its whip-crack song, often sung as a duet.

children.name: Psophodes olivaceus
children.description: The eastern whipbird (Psophodes olivaceus) is an insectivorous passerine bird native to the east coast of Australia.

children.name: Psophodes nigrogularis
children.description: The western whipbird (Psophodes nigrogularis) is a passerine bird found in several scattered populations in Southwest Australia.

children.name: Psophodes occidentalis
children.description: The chiming wedgebill (Psophodes occidentalis), sometimes referred to as chiming whipbird, is a species of bird in the family Psophodidae.

children.name: Sphenostoma
children.description: A monotypic genus of Australian bird with a distinctive wedge-shaped bill and loud, whistling calls. It inhabits arid and semi-arid scrublands.

children.name: Sphenostoma cristatum
children.description: A bird with a short crest, grey-brown upperparts, white throat, and black breast band. Its far-carrying, bell-like song is a characteristic sound of the Australian outback.

children.name: Coracina
children.description: A large genus of medium-sized birds with grey, black, and white plumage, found across Asia and Australasia. They are arboreal insectivores with a hooked bill.

children.name: Coracina melano
children.description: A cuckooshrike with grey upperparts, white underparts, and black wings. It is found in forests of South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Coracina novaeguineae
children.description: A cuckooshrike with grey upperparts, white underparts, and black wings. It is found in forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Coracina atakamensis
children.description: A cuckooshrike with dark grey plumage and a black mask. It is found in montane forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Pomatostomus
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, social birds with curved bills and brown and white plumage, found in Australia and New Guinea. They build large, dome-shaped communal nests.

children.name: Pomatostomus isidorei
children.description: The Papuan babbler (Garritornis isidorei), New Guinea babbler, or Isidore's rufous babbler, is a species of bird in the family Pomatostomidae.

children.name: Garrodia
children.description: A small genus of Asian babblers with plain brown plumage, found in forests of the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Garrodia subtilis
children.description: A plain brown babbler with a pale throat and belly, and a long tail. It is found in forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Garrodia leucocrypta
children.description: A babbler with a white breast and throat, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Modulatrix
children.description: A monotypic genus of thrush-like bird found in montane forests of eastern Africa.

children.name: Arcanator
children.description: A genus of two species of shy, thrush-like birds found in African montane forests.

children.name: Arcanator nigriceps
children.description: The Dusky Greenbul is a dark olive-brown bird with a blackish crown and pale eyes. It inhabits montane forests in the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania.

children.name: Promerops
children.description: A genus of long-tailed, nectar-feeding birds endemic to southern Africa.

children.name: Promerops cafer
children.description: The Cape sugarbird (Promerops cafer) is one of the eight bird species endemic to the Fynbos biome of the Western Cape and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa.

children.name: Irena
children.description: A genus of brilliantly blue and black passerines that feed primarily on fruit in tropical forests.

children.name: Irena puella
children.description: The Asian fairy-bluebird (Irena puella) is a medium-sized, arboreal passerine bird.

children.name: Elachura
children.description: A monotypic genus of small, dark, wren-like passerine found in Asian montane forests.

children.name: Elachura formosa
children.description: The spotted elachura or spotted wren-babbler (Elachura formosa) is a species of passerine bird found in the forests of the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Hyliota
children.description: A genus of small, active birds with blue-black or violet upperparts and pale underparts, found in African woodlands.

children.name: Hyliota australis
children.description: thumb|Southern Hyliota The southern hyliota (Hyliota australis) is a species of Hyliota.

children.name: Hyliota usambarae
children.description: The Usambara hyliota (Hyliota usambara) is a species of Hyliota.

children.name: Tichodroma
children.description: A monotypic genus of unique passerine adapted to climbing on vertical rock surfaces in mountainous regions.

children.name: Salpornis
children.description: A genus of bark-gleaning passerines with heavily spotted and barred plumage, found in Africa and India.

children.name: Salpornis spilonotus
children.description: The Indian spotted creeper (Salpornis spilonota) is a small passerine bird that is a member of the family Salpornithidae, which was previously treated as a subfamily of Certhiidae.

children.name: Buphagus
children.description: A genus of two species of tick-eating birds specialized for perching and foraging on large mammals.

children.name: Chloropsis
children.description: A genus of brilliantly green, warbler-like birds with blue, yellow, or orange facial markings, found across tropical Asia.

children.name: Chloropsis cochinchinensis
children.description: The Javan leafbird (Chloropsis cochinchinensis) is a species of leafbird found in old-growth and second growth forests in Java.

children.name: Chloropsis flavipennis
children.description: The Philippine leafbird (Chloropsis flavipennis) is a species of bird in the family Chloropseidae.

children.name: Chloropsis jerdoni
children.description: Jerdon's leafbird is a species of leafbird found in forest and woodland in India and Sri Lanka. Its name honours Thomas C. It has traditionally been considered a subspecies of the blue-winged leafbird, but differ in measurements and morphology, it lacking the blue flight feathers for which the blue-winged leafbird was named.

children.name: Chloropsis media
children.description: The Sumatran leafbird (Chloropsis media) is a species of bird in the family Chloropseidae.

children.name: Chloropsis nuttingi
children.description: A leafbird endemic to Mindanao.

children.name: Chloropsis zosterops
children.description: Chloropsis zosterops (Javan Leafbird) is a leafbirds species found in Asia region.

children.name: Dicaeum
children.description: The largest genus of flowerpeckers, with over 40 species of tiny, short-tailed birds found across Asia and Australasia.

children.name: Dicaeum bicolor
children.description: The bicolored flowerpecker (Dicaeum bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum concolor
children.description: The Nilgiri flowerpecker (Dicaeum concolor) is a tiny bird in the flowerpecker family.

children.name: Dicaeum erythrothorax
children.description: The Buru flowerpecker (Dicaeum erythrothorax) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum hyperthyroideum
children.description: A small flowerpecker with black breast band, endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicaeum hypoleucum
children.description: The buzzing flowerpecker or white-bellied flowerpecker is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It is endemic to the Philippines. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Dicaeum maugei
children.description: The red-chested flowerpecker or blue-cheeked flowerpecker is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It is found on the Lesser Sunda Islands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Dicaeum melanostethum
children.description: A flowerpecker with white streaking, endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicaeum minullum
children.description: The plain flowerpecker (Dicaeum minullum) is a bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum nitidum
children.description: The Louisiade flowerpecker (Dicaeum nitidum) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum proprium
children.description: The whiskered flowerpecker (Pachyglossa propria) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum pygmaeum
children.description: The pygmy flowerpecker (Dicaeum pygmaeum) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum quartum
children.description: A recently described flowerpecker from Mindanao in the Philippines.

children.name: Dicaeum reticulatum
children.description: A flowerpecker with golden rump, endemic to the island of Sumba, Indonesia.

children.name: Dicaeum sanctissimum
children.description: A flowerpecker with scarlet collar, endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicaeum sanguinolentum
children.description: The Javan flowerpecker (Dicaeum sanguinolentum), formerly named the blood-breasted flowerpecker, is a species of passerine bird in the flowerpecker family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum strangeri
children.description: A flowerpecker with white throat, endemic to the Moluccas.

children.name: Dicaeum teniolatum
children.description: A flowerpecker with white face mask, endemic to the Lesser Sunda Islands.

children.name: Dicaeum tristrami
children.description: The mottled flowerpecker or white-mottled flowerpecker (Dicaeum tristrami) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Dicaeum vulgare
children.description: A flowerpecker found on several islands in Wallacea.

children.name: Prionochilus
children.description: A genus of small flowerpeckers with thicker bills, found in Southeast Asia and the Philippines.

children.name: Prionochilus plateni
children.description: The Palawan flowerpecker (Prionochilus plateni) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.

children.name: Prionochilus aurifrons
children.description: A flowerpecker with golden forehead, endemic to Borneo.

children.name: Prionochilus johanniae
children.description: A flowerpecker with yellow rump, endemic to Borneo.

children.name: Prionochilus pectoralis
children.description: A flowerpecker with scarlet breast, endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Ploceus
children.description: A large genus of weavers with stout conical bills, known for their bright breeding plumages and woven nests.

children.name: Ploceus cucullatus
children.description: The village weaver (Ploceus cucullatus), also known as the spotted-backed weaver or black-headed weaver (the latter leading to easy confusion with P. melanocephalus), is a bird species in the family Ploceidae found in much of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Ploceus philippinus
children.description: The baya weaver (Ploceus philippinus) is a weaverbird found across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Ploceus aurantius
children.description: The orange weaver (Ploceus aurantius) is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus rubiginosus
children.description: The chestnut weaver (Ploceus rubiginosus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus baglafecht
children.description: The baglafecht weaver (Ploceus baglafecht) is a species of weaver bird from the family Ploceidae which is found in eastern and central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus nicolli
children.description: The Usambara weaver (Ploceus nicolli) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus capensis
children.description: The Cape weaver (Ploceus capensis) is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae, found in southern Africa.

children.name: Ploceus luchsingeri
children.description: A weaver with a yellow body, black face mask, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus ocularis
children.description: The spectacled weaver (Ploceus ocularis) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus manyar
children.description: The streaked weaver (Ploceus manyar) is a species of weaver bird found in South Asia and South-east Asia in the countries of Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam and also introduced in Qatar and United Arab Emirates (UAE).

children.name: Ploceus manucerus
children.description: A yellow weaver with an olive-green back and black bill. It is found in lowland forests and clearings of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus granulifrons
children.description: A weaver with a yellow body, black face, and a distinctive granular texture on the forehead. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus waldeni
children.description: A weaver with a yellow body, black crown, and olive upperparts. It is endemic to the island of Principe in the Gulf of Guinea.

children.name: Ploceus bahni
children.description: A weaver with a yellow body, black face, and olive upperparts. It is found in montane forests of Cameroon and Nigeria.

children.name: Anomalospiza
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Cuckoo Finch, a brood parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of cisticolas and prinias. It has a stout, conical bill and resembles a small weaver in appearance.

children.name: Quelea
children.description: A genus of small weavers that form some of the largest bird flocks on Earth.

children.name: Quelea cardinalis
children.description: The cardinal quelea (Quelea cardinalis) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Amblyospiza
children.description: A monotypic genus of large, thick-billed weaver found in African wetlands and forests.

children.name: Sporopipes
children.description: A small genus of small, finely patterned weavers with scalloped or spotted plumage. They are found in dry savannas and scrublands of Africa, building spherical grass nests in trees and bushes.

children.name: Philetairus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Sociable Weaver, famous for building enormous communal nests that resemble haystacks in trees and on utility poles. These structures are among the largest bird nests in the world and can house hundreds of birds.

children.name: Philetairus socius
children.description: The sociable weaver is a species of bird in the weaver family, endemic to Southern Africa. It is the only species in its genus Philetairus. It is found in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana, but its range is centered within the Northern Cape Province of South Africa.

children.name: Pseudonigrita
children.description: A small genus of social weavers that build their own nests, distinct from Philetairus but also highly gregarious. They inhabit dry savannas of eastern and southern Africa.

children.name: Malimbus
children.description: A genus of forest-dwelling weavers with bright red and black plumage, found in tropical Africa.

children.name: Malimbus ibadanensis
children.description: The Ibadan malimbe (Malimbus ibadanensis) is a rare species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Malimbus ballmanni
children.description: The Gola malimbe or Ballmann's malimbe (Malimbus ballmanni) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Malimbus malimbicus
children.description: The crested malimbe (Malimbus malimbicus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Bubalornis
children.description: A genus of large, heavy-billed weavers that build massive, untidy stick nests in trees. They are named for their association with African buffalo and other large mammals.

children.name: Dinemellia
children.description: A monotypic genus of weaver with a striking white head and black body, found in dry savannas of East Africa. It builds large, thorny stick nests in acacia trees.

children.name: Euplectes
children.description: A genus of weavers known as widowbirds and bishop birds, with males exhibiting striking elongated tail feathers and bright breeding plumage.

children.name: Euplectes capensis
children.description: The yellow bishop (Euplectes capensis), also known as Cape bishop, Cape widow or yellow-rumped widow, is a resident breeding Afromontane bird species.

children.name: Euplectes gierowii
children.description: The black bishop (Euplectes gierowii) is a species of passerine bird in the family Ploceidae native to Africa south of the Sahara.

children.name: Euplectes hartlaubi
children.description: The marsh widowbird or Hartlaub's widowbird (Euplectes hartlaubi) is a bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Euplectes psammocromius
children.description: The montane widowbird (Euplectes psammacromius), also known as the mountain marsh widowbird is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae, which is native to the eastern Afrotropics.

children.name: Plocepasser
children.description: A genus of social weavers that build large, compartmentalized communal nests, found in savannas of eastern and southern Africa.

children.name: Plocepasser ruficeps
children.description: A sparrow-weaver with a rufous crown, white eyebrow, brown upperparts, and white underparts. It is found in dry savannas of southern Africa.

children.name: Histurgops
children.description: A monotypic genus of large weaver with a distinctive rufous tail and heavily streaked plumage, endemic to Tanzania. It is a social species that builds messy nests in trees.

children.name: Histurgops crassirostris
children.description: A large weaver with a thick bill, streaked brown upperparts, white underparts, and a bright rufous tail. It is endemic to the savannas of central Tanzania.

children.name: Foudia
children.description: A genus of weavers endemic to the Indian Ocean islands of Madagascar, the Comoros, and the Seychelles. They are sometimes called fodies and are known for their bright red breeding plumage.

children.name: Foudia madagascariensis
children.description: The red fody (Foudia madagascariensis), also known as the Madagascar fody in Madagascar, red cardinal fody in Mauritius, or common fody, is a small bird native to Madagascar and introduced to various other islands in the Indian Ocean.

children.name: Foudia eminentissima
children.description: The Comoros fody (Foudia eminentissima), also known as the red-headed fody, is a species of passerine bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Foudia albicans
children.description: A fody with a red head and breast, white belly, and brown upperparts. It is endemic to the mountains of northern Madagascar.

children.name: Foudia flavicans
children.description: The Rodrigues fody (Foudia flavicans) is a rare species of bird in the weaver family.

children.name: Foudia rubra
children.description: The Mauritius fody (Foudia rubra) is a rare species of bird in the weaver family.

children.name: Foudia sechellarum
children.description: The Seychelles fody (Foudia sechellarum) is a small yellowish songbird that are native to the Seychelles islands of Cousin Island, Cousine Island, Frégate Island, and have been introduced to Aride Island, D'Arros Island and as of 2004 Denis Island.

children.name: Textor
children.description: A genus of forest-dwelling weavers with black and yellow plumage, found in Central and West Africa.

children.name: Textor capitalis
children.description: A forest weaver with a black head, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Textor albiventris
children.description: A forest weaver with a black head, white belly, yellow breast, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of West Africa.

children.name: Sitagra
children.description: A genus of bright yellow weavers with black or olive heads, found in wetlands and savannas of Africa.

children.name: Sitagra flavoviridis
children.description: A weaver with yellow-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a black bill. It is found in marshes and wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Sitagra luteola
children.description: A small weaver with yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a pale bill. It is found in wetlands and grasslands of western Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus
children.description: A genus of predominantly black weavers with red or yellow markings, found in forests of Central Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus nigerrimus
children.description: A glossy black weaver with a pale eye, found in lowland forests of central and western Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus albinuchus
children.description: A black weaver with a white nape patch, found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Oriolops
children.description: A genus of weavers with bright yellow and black plumage resembling orioles, found in forests of Africa.

children.name: Oriolops aurantius
children.description: A brilliant orange-and-black weaver found in mangroves and coastal forests of West Africa.

children.name: Oriolops sulphureus
children.description: A weaver with sulphur-yellow underparts, black head, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis
children.description: A genus of masked weavers with black face masks and bright yellow bodies, found across Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis velatus
children.description: A masked weaver with black face, yellow body, and olive back. It is common across southern Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis nigriceps
children.description: A masked weaver with a black head, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in savannas of East Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis taenioptera
children.description: A masked weaver with a black face mask, yellow body, and brown back. It is found in the Sahel region of Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus
children.description: A genus of small weavers with slender bills, found in forests and wetlands of Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus pelzelni
children.description: A small weaver with a slender bill, yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a black face mask. It is found in marshes of western and central Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus xanthopterus
children.description: A weaver with a brown throat, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in wetlands of southern Africa.

children.name: Nelicurvius
children.description: A genus of weavers found on the Mascarene Islands, with red and black plumage in males and brown in females.

children.name: Nelicurvius flavicans
children.description: A small fody with yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a red bill. It is endemic to Rodrigues Island.

children.name: Nelicurvius ruber
children.description: A small fody with red head and breast in males, brown upperparts, and a red bill. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Ploceus
children.description: Additional species of typical weavers from Africa and Asia, known for their bright breeding plumages and woven nests.

children.name: Ploceus flavovirens
children.description: A weaver with yellow-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a black bill. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus melanoxanthus
children.description: A weaver with a black head and breast, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus nigriventris
children.description: A weaver with a black belly, yellow breast and throat, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus rufaxillaris
children.description: A weaver with rufous wing patches, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in savannas of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus fuscus
children.description: A dark weaver with brownish-black plumage and a pale eye. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus melanospiza
children.description: A weaver with a black bill, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in marshes of East Africa.

children.name: Ploceus cinnabarinus
children.description: A weaver with a bright cinnabar-red breast and belly, black head, and olive back. It is found in marshes of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus aurantiacus
children.description: A weaver with an orange back and rump, black head, and yellow underparts. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus chrysopterus
children.description: A weaver with golden-yellow wing patches, black head, and yellow body. It is found in wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus erythrops
children.description: A weaver with a red face and throat, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of West Africa.

children.name: Ploceus sulfuraceus
children.description: A weaver with sulphur-yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a black bill. It is found in wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus luteolus
children.description: The little weaver (Ploceus luteolus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus micropteryx
children.description: A weaver with a black head, yellow body, and relatively small wings. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus albiventris
children.description: A weaver with a black head, white belly, yellow breast, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus flavicans
children.description: A weaver with a yellow back and rump, black head, and yellow underparts. It is found in savannas of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus castaneiceps
children.description: The Taveta weaver (Ploceus castaneiceps), also known as the Taveta golden weaver, (or the mango bird) is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae.

children.name: Anomalospiza
children.description: Anomalospiza — a genus of indigobirds & whydahs in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Anomalospiza imberbis
children.description: The cuckoo-finch, also known as the parasitic weaver or cuckoo weaver, is a small passerine bird now placed in the family Viduidae with the indigobirds and whydahs. It occurs in grassland in Africa south of the Sahara. The male is mainly yellow and green while the female is buff with dark streaks.

children.name: Vidua
children.description: A genus of brood-parasitic finch-like birds with striking sexual dimorphism and long tail feathers in breeding males.

children.name: Vidua chalybeata
children.description: The village indigobird (Vidua chalybeata), also known as the steelblue widowfinch or (in U.S.

children.name: Vidua larvaticola
children.description: The barka indigobird (Vidua larvaticola) is a species of bird in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Vidua nigeriae
children.description: The quailfinch indigobird (Vidua nigeriae) is a small songbird.

children.name: Vidua purpurascens
children.description: The purple indigobird (Vidua purpurascens) is a species of bird in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Vidua raricola
children.description: The jambandu indigobird (Vidua raricola) is a species of bird in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Vidua camerunensis
children.description: The Cameroon indigobird (Vidua camerunensis) is a species of bird in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Vidua funerea
children.description: :The name dusky indigobird can also refer to Vidua purpurascens.

children.name: Vidua codringtoni
children.description: The Zambezi indigobird (Vidua codringtoni), also known as the twinspot indigobird or green indigobird, is a species of bird in the family Viduidae.

children.name: Peucedramus
children.description: A monotypic genus of warbler-like passerine endemic to highland pine forests of North and Central America.

children.name: Peucedramus taeniatus
children.description: The olive warbler (Peucedramus taeniatus) is a small passerine bird.

children.name: Urocynchramus
children.description: A monotypic genus of long-tailed finch-like bird endemic to the mountains of central China.

children.name: Plectrophenax
children.description: A genus of largely white buntings that breed in high Arctic regions and winter in temperate zones.

children.name: Plectrophenax nivalis
children.description: The snow bunting is a passerine bird in the family Calcariidae. It is an Arctic specialist, with a circumpolar Arctic breeding range throughout the northern hemisphere. There are small isolated populations on a few high mountain tops south of the Arctic region, including the Cairngorms in central Scotland and the Saint Elias Mountains on the southern Alaska-Yukon border, as well as the Cape Breton Highlands.

children.name: Calcarius
children.description: A genus of sparrow-like birds with elongated hind claws, found in open habitats of the Northern Hemisphere.

children.name: Calcarius lapponicus
children.description: The Lapland longspur, also known as the Lapland bunting, is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae. It is a circumpolar arctic breeder and the only member of the genus Calcarius present in Eurasia.

children.name: Calcarius bicolor
children.description: A large, robust longspur with a thick, conical bill, a black-and-white head pattern, and chestnut nape in breeding males, found on the Arctic tundra of Canada and wintering in the central grasslands of the United States. It is distinguished from other longspurs by its heavier bill and more deliberate movements.

children.name: Rhodinocichla
children.description: A monotypic genus of striking passerine with unclear taxonomic affinities, found in Central and South America.

children.name: Zonotrichia
children.description: A genus of large, handsome sparrows with distinctive crown patterns, found across North America.

children.name: Zonotrichia leucophrys
children.description: The white-crowned sparrow is a species of passerine bird native to North America. A medium-sized member of the New World sparrow family, this species is marked by a grey face and black and white streaking on the upper head. It breeds in brushy areas in the taiga and tundra of the northernmost parts of the continent and in the Rocky Mountains and Pacific coast.

children.name: Zonotrichia spathz
children.description: This newly described species, Zonotrichia spathz, is a small passerine bird known for its distinct song and preference for forested habitats.

children.name: Melospiza
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, heavily streaked sparrows found across North America.

children.name: Melospiza melodia
children.description: The song sparrow is a medium-sized New World sparrow. Among the native sparrows in North America, it is easily one of the most abundant, variable, and adaptable species.

children.name: Melospiza georgiana
children.description: The swamp sparrow (Melospiza georgiana) is a medium-sized New World sparrow related to the song sparrow.

children.name: Centronyx
children.description: A small genus of grassland sparrows formerly placed in Ammodramus, found in the prairies of North America.

children.name: Spizella
children.description: A genus of small, slender sparrows with rufous crowns and plain underparts, found across North America.

children.name: Spizella passerina
children.description: The chipping sparrow (Spizella passerina) is a species of New World sparrow, a passerine bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Spizella pusilla
children.description: The field sparrow is a small New World sparrow in the family Passerellidae. It is about 140 mm (6 in) long and weighs about 12.5 g (0.4 oz). The head is grey with a rust-coloured crown, white eye-ring and pink bill.

children.name: Junco
children.description: A genus of sparrows with grey or brown plumage and white outer tail feathers, found across North America.

children.name: Junco vulcani
children.description: The volcano junco (Junco vulcani) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Junco insularis
children.description: The Guadalupe junco (Junco insularis) is a small bird in the New World sparrow family that is endemic to Guadalupe Island off the western coast of Baja California, Mexico.

children.name: Passerella
children.description: A genus of large, heavily built sparrows with variable rufous and grey plumage.

children.name: Passerella iliaca
children.description: The fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca) is a large New World sparrow.

children.name: Peucaea
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with stout bills and often rufous wings, found in arid and semi-arid habitats from the southern United States through Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Artemisiospiza
children.description: A genus of pale, desert-dwelling sparrows formerly placed in Amphispiza, found in sagebrush and saltbush habitats of western North America.

children.name: Artemisiospiza nevadensis
children.description: The sagebrush sparrow (Artemisiospiza nevadensis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Pooecetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Vesper Sparrow, a long-bodied sparrow of open grasslands and fields across North America.

children.name: Pooecetes gramineus
children.description: The vesper sparrow (Pooecetes gramineus) is a medium-sized New World sparrow.

children.name: Passerculus
children.description: A widespread genus of small, streaked sparrows found in grasslands across North America. The Savannah Sparrow complex shows remarkable variation across subspecies, some of which were once considered separate species.

children.name: Passerculus sandwichensis
children.description: The Savannah sparrow is a small New World sparrow that is the only member of the genus Passerculus. It is a widespread and abundant species that occupies open grassland habitats in North America.

children.name: Ammodramus
children.description: A genus of chunky, short-tailed sparrows adapted to dense grasslands, found across North America. They are notoriously secretive and are more often heard than seen, but their insect-like songs carry far across open fields.

children.name: Ammodramus savannarum
children.description: The grasshopper sparrow (Ammodramus savannarum) is a small New World sparrow.

children.name: Ammodramus humeralis
children.description: The grassland sparrow (Ammodramus humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Ammospiza
children.description: A genus of sparrows specialised for life in coastal salt marshes, tidal creeks, and brackish wetlands along the coasts of North America. They have distinctive, rather flat heads and stout bills adapted for a diet of small crustaceans and insects in addition to seeds.

children.name: Ammospiza maritima
children.description: The seaside sparrow (Ammospiza maritima) is a species of American sparrow.

children.name: Ammospiza caudacuta
children.description: The saltmarsh sparrow (Ammospiza caudacuta) is a small New World sparrow found in salt marshes along the Atlantic coast of the United States.

children.name: Pipilo
children.description: A genus of large, handsome sparrows known as towhees, characterised by long tails, stout bills, and striking plumage patterns. They are primarily ground-foraging birds that scratch loudly through leaf litter with both feet in a backwards hop.

children.name: Pipilo maculatus
children.description: The spotted towhee (Pipilo maculatus) is a large New World sparrow.

children.name: Pipilo erythrophthalmus
children.description: The eastern towhee, also known as chewink, joree, or joree bird, is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been under debate in recent decades, and formerly this bird and the spotted towhee were considered a single species, the rufous-sided towhee.

children.name: Pipilo ocai
children.description: The collared towhee (Pipilo ocai) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Melozone
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with often plain brown or strikingly patterned plumage, found from the southwestern United States through Mexico to Central America.

children.name: Melozone crissalis
children.description: The California towhee (Melozone crissalis) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to the coastal regions of western Oregon and California in the United States and Baja California and Baja California Sur in Mexico.

children.name: Melozone fusca
children.description: The canyon towhee (Melozone fusca) is a bird of the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Aimophila
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with long tails and rusty crowns, found in arid and semi-arid scrublands from the southwestern United States through Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Aimophila notosticta
children.description: The Oaxaca sparrow (Aimophila notosticta) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Amphispiza
children.description: A small genus of pale, desert-dwelling sparrows with striking facial patterns. They are well adapted to arid environments and are characteristic birds of the deserts and dry scrublands of western North America.

children.name: Chondestes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Lark Sparrow, one of the most distinctive North American sparrows with a striking facial pattern of chestnut, black, and white. It has a long, rounded tail and a stout seed-cracking bill.

children.name: Chondestes grammacus
children.description: The lark sparrow (Chondestes grammacus) is a fairly large New World sparrow.

children.name: Rhynchospiza
children.description: A small genus of sparrows found in arid and semi-arid scrublands of western South America. They were formerly included in Aimophila and have stout, conical bills adapted for seed-cracking.

children.name: Rhynchospiza strigiceps
children.description: | range_map = Rhynchospiza strigiceps map.svg.

children.name: Pezopetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Large-footed Finch, a large, terrestrial sparrow of montane forests in Central America. It is named for its unusually large, powerful feet adapted for scratching through leaf litter.

children.name: Torreornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Zapata Sparrow, a secretive, ground-dwelling sparrow endemic to Cuba and one of the most restricted-range passerines in the Americas.

children.name: Xenospiza
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Sierra Madre Sparrow, a highly range-restricted species endemic to highland grasslands of Mexico. It is threatened by habitat loss and agricultural intensification.

children.name: Arremonops
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, olive-backed sparrows with striped heads, found from southern Texas through Mexico and Central America to northern South America.

children.name: Arremonops rufivirgatus
children.description: The olive sparrow (Arremonops rufivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Arremon
children.description: A genus of sparrows and brush finches with striking black, white, and olive plumage patterns, found from Mexico through Central and South America. They inhabit forest undergrowth and are often more easily heard than seen.

children.name: Arremon laniirostris
children.description: A dull olive-brown brush finch with a grey head, pale throat, and a stout black bill. It ranges from Costa Rica through Central America to western Ecuador in humid lowland and premontane forests.

children.name: Atlapetes
children.description: A large genus of colorful brush finches with rufous, yellow, and olive plumage, found in montane forests and scrublands of Central and South America. They are active, often conspicuous birds that forage in pairs or small groups.

children.name: Atlapetes personatus
children.description: The tepui brushfinch (Atlapetes personatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Atlapetes canigenis
children.description: The Cuzco brushfinch (Atlapetes canigenis), also known as the grey brushfinch or sooty brushfinch, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Atlapetes schistaceus
children.description: The slaty brushfinch or northern slaty brushfinch (Atlapetes schistaceus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Atlapetes tricolor
children.description: The tricolored brushfinch or golden-crowned brushfinch (Atlapetes tricolor) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Chlorospingus
children.description: A genus of small, olive-and-yellow birds formerly placed in the tanager family but now considered New World sparrows. They are active, social birds of montane forests from Mexico to South America.

children.name: Chlorospingus novaeguineae
children.description: A bush tanager with olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a blackish crown. It is found in the Darien highlands of Panama and Colombia.

children.name: Oreothraupis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Tanager Finch, a distinctive bird with a thick bill and striking black-and-white head pattern. It was once considered a tanager but is now placed in the New World sparrow family.

children.name: Oreothraupis arremonops
children.description: | range_map = Oreothraupis arremonops map.svg.

children.name: Pipilopsis
children.description: A small genus of sparrows with boldly striped heads, found in the Andes of South America.

children.name: Pipilopsis leucoptera
children.description: A sparrow with a black-and-white striped head, olive-brown upperparts, and white underparts. It is found in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Pipilopsis boliviana
children.description: A sparrow with a striped head, brown upperparts, and pale underparts. It is endemic to the highlands of Bolivia.

children.name: Haplospiza
children.description: A small genus of finches with uniformly dark grey or slaty plumage in males, found in Central and South America. They inhabit forest edges and clearings, feeding on grass seeds and bamboo seeds.

children.name: Haplospiza unicolor
children.description: The uniform finch (Haplospiza unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

children.name: Haplospiza rustica
children.description: The slaty finch (Haplospiza rustica) is a bird species in the family Thraupidae (formerly in Emberizidae).

children.name: Acanthidops
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Peg-billed Finch, a distinctive bird of high-altitude scrub in Central America. It has a uniquely shaped, upturned bill adapted for extracting seeds from bamboo flowers.

children.name: Acanthidops barbatus
children.description: A small finch with a distinctive pale, upturned bill, grey upperparts, white underparts, and white outer tail feathers. It is found in highland scrub and bamboo thickets of Costa Rica and western Panama.

children.name: Spizellopsis
children.description: A genus of finches with streaked brown plumage, found in grasslands and open habitats of South America.

children.name: Spizellopsis brunneiventris
children.description: A finch with streaked brown upperparts, brownish underparts, and a pale supercilium. It is found in grasslands of southern South America.

children.name: Geospizopsis
children.description: A genus of plain-coloured finches found in the high Andes of South America, with grey or brown plumage and conical bills.

children.name: Geospizopsis plumbea
children.description: A finch with lead-grey plumage, a black bill, and white outer tail feathers. It is found in the high Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Phrygilus
children.description: A genus of finches with grey, black, and white plumage, found in the high Andes of South America. They inhabit rocky slopes and dry scrub at high elevations.

children.name: Phrygilus atacamensis
children.description: A finch with a grey head, yellow underparts, and brown back. It is found in the arid highlands of Chile and Argentina.

children.name: Oryzoborus
children.description: A genus of finches with massive, thick bills adapted for cracking hard seeds, found in wet lowlands of Central and South America. They are sometimes placed in the tanager family but are now considered New World sparrows.

children.name: Volatinia
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Blue-black Grassquit, a small finch of open and semi-open habitats in Central and South America. Males are glossy blue-black during the breeding season.

children.name: Sporophila
children.description: A large genus of small, seed-eating finches with thick conical bills, found across Central and South America. Males often have striking black, white, and chestnut plumage patterns, while females are drab brown. Many species are popular cage birds.

children.name: Sporophila corvina
children.description: The variable seedeater (Sporophila corvina) is a passerine bird which breeds from southern Mexico through Central America to the Chocó of northwestern South America.

children.name: Sporophila muralata
children.description: A small seedeater with black and white plumage, found in grasslands of southeastern Colombia.

children.name: Sporophila bouvreuil
children.description: The copper seedeater (Sporophila bouvreuil) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

children.name: Sporophila nigra
children.description: A seedeater with completely black plumage in males, brown in females. It is endemic to the Antilles.

children.name: Sporophila albicauda
children.description: A seedeater with a black head, white tail, grey back, and white underparts. It is found in grasslands of central South America.

children.name: Sporophila palustris
children.description: The marsh seedeater (Sporophila palustris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

children.name: Sporophila cinerea
children.description: A seedeater with grey upperparts, white underparts, and a stout grey bill. It is found in grasslands of South America.

children.name: Sporophila melanocephala
children.description: A seedeater with a black head, rufous breast, grey back, and white belly. It is found in grasslands of southern South America.

children.name: Sporophila pilzei
children.description: A seedeater with a black head and breast, grey back, and white belly. It is endemic to the Cerrado region of Brazil.

children.name: Calyptophilus
children.description: A genus of two species of thrush-like tanagers endemic to Hispaniola.

children.name: Phaenicophilus
children.description: A genus of two species of tanager with black crowns and pale underparts, endemic to Hispaniola.

children.name: Xenoligea
children.description: A monotypic genus of warbler-like tanager endemic to the montane forests of Hispaniola.

children.name: Microligea
children.description: A monotypic genus of small, warbler-like bird endemic to Hispaniola.

children.name: Nesospingus
children.description: A monotypic genus of tanager endemic to Puerto Rico's montane forests.

children.name: Spindalis
children.description: A genus of brightly colored birds with bold head patterns, endemic to the Caribbean islands.

children.name: Spindalis zena
children.description: The western spindalis (Spindalis zena) is a songbird species.

children.name: Spindalis nigricephala
children.description: The Jamaican spindalis (Spindalis nigricephala) is one of four species of bird in family Spindalidae.

children.name: Spindalis dominicensis
children.description: The Hispaniolan spindalis (Spindalis dominicensis) is one of four species of bird in family Spindalidae.

children.name: Zeledonia
children.description: A monotypic genus of small, dark, wren-like bird endemic to the Talamancan montane forests.

children.name: Teretistris
children.description: A genus of two warbler species endemic to Cuba, with plain grey-brown and yellow plumage.

children.name: Teretistris fornsi
children.description: The Oriente warbler (Teretistris fornsi) is one of two species of bird in the Cuban warbler family Teretistridae.

children.name: Icteria
children.description: A monotypic genus of large, thick-billed warbler found in dense thickets across North America.

children.name: Mitrospingus
children.description: A genus of two tanager species with olive upperparts and distinctive facial patterns.

children.name: Lamprospiza
children.description: A monotypic genus of striking black, white, and red tanager found in Amazonian forests.

children.name: Orthogonys
children.description: A monotypic genus of olive-green tanager with white wing patches, endemic to southeastern Brazil.
